entries.1:1: This book is a collection of wise sayings from Solomon, the son of David and king of Israel. It tells the reader where these lessons come from and invites them to take the advice seriously.
entries.1:2: The purpose of these sayings is to teach you wise ways of living and help you understand words that make good sense. Reading them can make your thinking clearer and more careful.
entries.1:3: These lessons train you to live rightly, to judge fairly, and to act honestly. They are meant to shape how you treat other people day by day.
entries.1:4: This teaching helps people who are naive become sharp and gives young people knowledge and a serious sense of purpose. It is especially useful for those still learning how to make good choices.
entries.1:5: Even a wise person can learn more by listening, and a sensible person can become even better guided. No one is too smart to benefit from these sayings.
entries.1:6: These proverbs help you grasp the meaning of wise sayings, riddles, and hard-to-understand words from the wise. With practice, you can understand lessons that are not obvious at first.
entries.1:7: Respecting the Lord and taking him seriously is where real knowledge begins, but foolish people refuse wisdom and correction. If you want to learn, start by honoring God rather than dismissing what he says.
entries.1:8: Listen to your father's instruction and don't reject your mother's teaching. The people who raised you often have lessons worth keeping.
entries.1:9: Good teaching from your parents is like a crown on your head and a fine necklace around your neck. It adds honor and beauty to your life when you accept it.
entries.1:10: If sinful people try to pull you off the right path, don't go along with them. It is wiser to refuse than to follow friends into trouble.
entries.1:11: They may invite you to join them in plotting against innocent people and ambushing them for no reason. Their plan sounds exciting, but it is aimed at harming others.
entries.1:12: They talk about swallowing people up alive and sending them down to death, as if their victims were nothing. Their words show how little they care about human life.
entries.1:13: They promise that you will get valuable goods and fill your houses with wealth. They use the lure of easy money to draw you in.
entries.1:14: They ask you to throw in your lot with them and share one money bag. They make it sound like everyone will profit together, but it is a trap.
entries.1:15: Don't walk with such people or follow their path. Stay away from them, even if they seem friendly.
entries.1:16: They are quick to run toward evil and ready to take a life. Their feet are already headed in a violent direction.
entries.1:17: A bird that sees a net set out will not fly into it, so setting a trap in plain sight is pointless. In the same way, these people are blind to the trap they are setting for themselves.
entries.1:18: They lie in wait for others' blood, but they are really preparing disaster for themselves. The harm they plan comes back on them.
entries.1:19: This is what happens to everyone greedy for dishonest gain: it takes away the life of those who chase it. Money gained by harming others ends up costing you more than it gives.
entries.1:20: Wisdom is pictured as a woman crying out in the streets and raising her voice in public places. God's wisdom is not hidden; it is offered openly to everyone.
entries.1:21: She calls out where people gather and at the city gates, the busiest spots. Wisdom speaks right where everyday decisions are made.
entries.1:22: Wisdom asks how long naive people will love foolishness, mockers will enjoy their pride, and fools will hate knowledge. She is urging them to stop and change before it is too late.
entries.1:23: If you turn back and respond to her correction, she promises to pour out her spirit on you and make her words clear. Wisdom is ready to help anyone willing to listen and change.
entries.1:24: But they ignored her call and paid no attention when she reached out to them. Refusing wisdom has consequences.
entries.1:25: They rejected her guidance and wanted nothing to do with her correction. They chose their own way over being taught.
entries.1:26: So when trouble comes, wisdom will laugh and mock their fear. This is a strong picture of what it looks like to be left without help after ignoring good advice.
entries.1:27: Their fear will hit like a storm and their trouble like a rushing wind, bringing pain and sorrow. The disaster they ignored will finally arrive.
entries.1:28: Then they will call, but wisdom will not answer; they will search for her but not find her. A time comes when the chance to learn has passed.
entries.1:29: The reason is that they hated knowledge and did not set their hearts on respecting the Lord. They rejected the very thing that would have helped them.
entries.1:30: They wanted none of her teaching and treated her warnings as worthless. They turned down every chance to be corrected.
entries.1:31: So they will have to eat the fruit of their own choices and be filled with what their plans produce. What you plant eventually becomes what you live on.
entries.1:32: Naive people who turn away from wisdom bring about their own death, and the false peace of fools destroys them. Feeling safe while ignoring good advice is dangerous.
entries.1:33: But whoever listens to wisdom will rest securely, live in peace, and not be afraid of evil. Paying attention to wisdom brings safety and calm.
entries.2:1: This is a father urging his child to really take good advice to heart and remember it. It means you should value wise teaching enough to hold onto it, not just hear it once and forget it.
entries.2:2: You have to actually pay attention and want to learn, not just let wisdom go in one ear and out the other. It means leaning in with your ears and your heart when good teaching comes your way.
entries.2:3: Wisdom is worth asking for out loud, like something you really need. It means you should pray and actively seek understanding instead of waiting for it to just happen.
entries.2:4: You should hunt for wisdom the way people dig for silver or search for hidden treasure. It means treating understanding as something valuable enough to work hard for.
entries.2:5: When you seek wisdom like that, you come to understand what it means to respect the Lord and to actually know God. It means real knowledge of God grows out of a genuine search for it.
entries.2:6: Wisdom doesn't come from us; God is the one who gives it, and real knowledge and understanding come from him. It means when you find wisdom, you should thank God for it rather than pat yourself on the back.
entries.2:7: God has help ready for people who live honestly, and he protects those who mean well. It means doing right isn't wasted; God stands guard over you.
entries.2:8: God watches over the paths of people who do right and looks after those who respect him. It means you are not walking through life unnoticed or unprotected.
entries.2:9: With wisdom you learn what is fair and right and how to live well in every situation. It means good sense shows you the right way to act, not just the right facts to know.
entries.2:10: Wisdom settles into your heart and knowing what's right becomes something you actually enjoy. It means the goal is to love what is good, not just obey it reluctantly.
entries.2:11: Good judgment and understanding will guard you like a watchman. It means wisdom protects you from bad choices before you even make them.
entries.2:12: Wisdom will keep you away from harmful people and from those who lie. It means good sense helps you spot and avoid people who would lead you astray.
entries.2:13: These are people who walk away from doing right and choose crooked, hidden paths instead. It means watch out for those who quietly abandon honesty.
entries.2:14: They actually enjoy doing wrong and get a kick out of others' bad plans. It means be wary of people who treat evil as fun.
entries.2:15: Their paths are twisted and their steps lead toward evil. It means their way of life looks off-course, and following it takes you somewhere bad.
entries.2:16: Wisdom also saves you from a seductive woman who uses flattery to trap you. It means smooth, charming words can be a warning sign, not a compliment.
entries.2:17: She has betrayed her husband and forgotten the promises she made before God. It means breaking a commitment to God and to people is serious, and it leads to harm.
entries.2:18: Her house is a road that leads down to death and the grave. It means going along with her leads somewhere that ruins life, not somewhere good.
entries.2:19: People who go to her rarely come back; they don't find their way to life again. It means this path is a trap that is very hard to escape.
entries.2:20: The point of all this is that you would walk the good road and follow the example of honest people. It means wisdom is meant to shape how you live, day by day.
entries.2:21: People who live honestly will stay in the land, and good people will keep it as their own. It means integrity leads to lasting security.
entries.2:22: But those who do wrong will be removed from the land, and liars will be pulled up by the roots. It means evil doesn't last; it eventually gets cleared away.
entries.3:1: This is advice from a parent figure to remember good teaching and hold it close in your heart. It means you should let wise instruction shape who you are, not just hear it once and forget it.
entries.3:2: Following this teaching brings a longer, fuller life and peace. The point is that living wisely tends to make life better and calmer for you.
entries.3:3: Don't let kindness and faithfulness slip away from you; keep them always with you and written on your heart. It means making loyalty and mercy a constant part of your character.
entries.3:4: If you live this way, you will find favor and a good reputation with both God and people. It means your character will earn you trust and respect.
entries.3:5: Trust God with your whole heart instead of relying only on your own understanding. It means leaning on God when you can't figure everything out yourself.
entries.3:6: In everything you do, pay attention to God, and he will guide your path straight. It means letting God direct your decisions rather than going it alone.
entries.3:7: Don't think you're wise enough on your own; instead, respect God and turn away from evil. It means staying humble and letting reverence for God keep you from doing wrong.
entries.3:8: This kind of humility and reverence brings health to your body and strength to your bones. It means that living rightly is good for you, inside and out.
entries.3:9: Honor God with your money and give him the first share of what you earn. It means putting God first with your resources, not just your words.
entries.3:10: If you do this, your barns will be full and your supplies will overflow. It means generosity toward God is pictured as leading to abundance and provision.
entries.3:11: Don't resent it when the Lord corrects you or resist his discipline. It means accepting correction as something meant to help you grow, not hurt you.
entries.3:12: The Lord corrects those he loves, the way a father corrects a son he delights in. It means hard lessons can be a sign of God's care, not rejection.
entries.3:13: The person who finds wisdom and gains understanding is truly happy. It means real joy comes from learning to live well and wisely.
entries.3:14: Wisdom is worth more than silver or gold as an investment. It means gaining understanding pays off more than chasing money.
entries.3:15: Wisdom is more precious than jewels, and nothing you could want compares to it. It means wisdom is the most valuable thing you can pursue.
entries.3:16: Wisdom offers long life in one hand and wealth and honor in the other. It means wisdom is pictured as bringing lasting benefits with it.
entries.3:17: Wisdom's paths are pleasant, and her ways lead to peace. It means following wisdom makes life enjoyable and calm rather than harsh and stressful.
entries.3:18: Wisdom is like a tree of life to those who hold on to her, and those who keep her are happy. It means wisdom gives life and joy to those who treasure it.
entries.3:19: The Lord used wisdom to lay the foundations of the earth and understanding to set the heavens in place. It means wisdom is at the heart of how God made and orders everything.
entries.3:20: By his knowledge the deep waters were divided and the dew fell from the sky. It means God's understanding is behind the natural world and its provision.
entries.3:21: Hold on to good sense and sound judgment; don't let them out of your sight. It means staying clear-headed and purposeful in how you live.
entries.3:22: These things will be life to your soul and an ornament of grace around your neck. It means good judgment brings inner vitality and makes your character attractive.
entries.3:23: Then you will walk safely on your way, and your feet won't stumble. It means living wisely helps you avoid unnecessary falls and dangers.
entries.3:24: When you lie down, you won't be afraid, and your sleep will be sweet. It means wisdom brings peace of mind that lets you rest.
entries.3:25: Don't be terrified by sudden disaster or the ruin that comes on those who do evil. It means you don't have to live in fear of every crisis.
entries.3:26: The Lord will be your confidence and will keep your foot from being caught in a trap. It means God is your safety when trouble comes.
entries.3:27: Don't hold back good from people who deserve it when you have the power to help. It means do good now when it's in your hands to do so.
entries.3:28: Don't tell your neighbor to come back tomorrow when you already have what they need today. It means don't delay help you could give right now.
entries.3:29: Don't plot harm against a neighbor who lives near you without suspicion. It means don't betray the trust of people who live peacefully alongside you.
entries.3:30: Don't start a quarrel or lawsuit with someone who hasn't wronged you. It means don't pick fights with people who have done you no harm.
entries.3:31: Don't envy a violent person or copy any of their ways. It means don't admire or imitate people who get ahead by force.
entries.3:32: The Lord detests the crooked person but is a close friend to the upright. It means God opposes dishonesty and stands with those who live honestly.
entries.3:33: The Lord's curse is on the home of the wicked, but his blessing is on the home of the upright. It means the way you live affects the household you build.
entries.3:34: He mocks the proud but gives grace to the humble. It means God resists arrogance but shows kindness to those who are lowly in heart.
entries.3:35: The wise will inherit honor, but foolishness brings shame. It means wisdom leads to lasting respect, while foolish choices end in disgrace.
entries.4:1: A father is asking his children to listen carefully to what he teaches them. It means for us that we should pay attention to good advice so we can actually learn from it.
entries.4:2: The father says his teaching is genuinely good and worth keeping. For the reader, it means don't throw away sound instruction you've been given.
entries.4:3: He remembers being a young son himself, loved and cared for by his parents. It reminds us that wisdom is passed down through family and those who raised us.
entries.4:4: His father taught him to hold on to his words and rules so he could live well. It means taking good teaching to heart can lead to a better life.
entries.4:5: He urges us to go after wisdom and understanding and never walk away from it. For the reader, it means making wisdom something you actively pursue, not just admire.
entries.4:6: If you don't abandon wisdom, it will protect you; loving it keeps you safe. It means the effort you put into wisdom pays you back with protection.
entries.4:7: The most important thing about wisdom is actually getting it, even if it costs you everything. For the reader, it means wisdom is worth more than anything else you could spend on.
entries.4:8: If you value wisdom highly, it will raise you up and bring you honour. It means treating wisdom as precious leads to respect and a better standing.
entries.4:9: Wisdom will make you beautiful and honoured, like a crown on your head. For the reader, it means wisdom adds dignity and grace to your life.
entries.4:10: The father asks his son to listen and take his words to heart, promising a long life. It means paying attention to good teaching can lead to a fuller, longer life.
entries.4:11: He has taught his son the way of wisdom and set him on a straight path. For the reader, it means good teaching gives you clear direction for how to live.
entries.4:12: If you follow wisdom, your path won't be blocked and you won't stumble when you run. It means living wisely makes your way smoother and safer.
entries.4:13: Hold tightly to instruction and never let it go, because it is your life. For the reader, it means good teaching is essential, so guard it carefully.
entries.4:14: Don't walk on the path that sinners and evil people take. It means choose your company and your direction carefully, avoiding the way of wrongdoing.
entries.4:15: Stay far away from that evil path, turn from it, and keep going on your own way. For the reader, it means don't flirt with temptation; avoid it completely.
entries.4:16: Evil people can't rest until they've done wrong and caused someone to fall. It means wrongdoing becomes a restless habit that drives people to keep hurting others.
entries.4:17: They feed on evil and drink violence, as if it were their daily bread and wine. For the reader, it means some people make wrongdoing their whole way of life.
entries.4:18: The path of good people is like the growing light of dawn, getting brighter until full daylight. It means living rightly leads to increasing clarity and hope.
entries.4:19: The path of sinners is dark, and they don't even see what makes them stumble. For the reader, it means wrongdoing blinds people to the harm they cause themselves.
entries.4:20: The father again asks his son to pay close attention to his words. It means we should listen carefully to good teaching rather than let it pass by.
entries.4:21: Keep those words in sight and hold them deep in your heart. For the reader, it means good teaching should stay before you and shape you from the inside.
entries.4:22: These words bring life and health to those who find them. It means taking good teaching to heart can benefit your whole self, body and life.
entries.4:23: What you let into your heart shapes your whole life. Guard it like something valuable.
entries.4:24: Get rid of crooked, dishonest speech and keep false words far from you. For the reader, it means watch what you say and refuse to lie or twist the truth.
entries.4:25: Look straight ahead at what is in front of you. It means stay focused on your path and don't let yourself be distracted.
entries.4:26: Watch carefully how you live and make sure your ways are right. For the reader, it means pay attention to your choices and keep your life in good order.
entries.4:27: Don't turn aside to the right or the left, and keep your feet away from evil. It means stay steady on the right path and don't wander into wrongdoing.
entries.5:1: A father is urging his son to really listen to wise advice and teaching. It means we should pay close attention when someone with wisdom tries to guide us.
entries.5:2: Listening to wisdom helps you live with good sense and speak what is true and right. It means the advice you take in shapes how you think and talk.
entries.5:3: A seductive woman talks sweetly and smoothly to draw a man in. It means temptation often looks and sounds very appealing at first.
entries.5:4: But in the end that sweet talk leads to something bitter and painful, cutting like a sharp blade. It means the pleasure of temptation does not last and ends up hurting you.
entries.5:5: Her path leads downward to death and the grave. It means following this temptation takes a person toward ruin.
entries.5:6: She does not stay on the path that leads to life; her ways are unstable and she ignores what is right. It means the person who tempts you is not leading you anywhere good.
entries.5:7: The father again tells his sons to listen and not turn away from his words. It means we should hold on to good advice instead of ignoring it.
entries.5:8: Stay far away from her and don't even go near her house. It means the safest way to beat temptation is to keep your distance from it.
entries.5:9: If you don't, you will hand over your honor and your hard-earned money to others. It means giving in to this temptation costs you your reputation and your resources.
entries.5:10: Other people will end up enjoying the wealth you worked for. It means the cost of this sin is that strangers benefit from what you built.
entries.5:11: At the end of your life you will be full of grief as your body wastes away. It means you will look back with deep regret over what you lost.
entries.5:12: You will say to yourself that you hated instruction and set no value on being corrected. It means regret comes from ignoring the guidance you were given.
entries.5:13: You will admit you did not listen to your teachers or pay attention to those guiding you. It means refusing good advice leaves you wishing you had listened.
entries.5:14: You will realize you were almost completely ruined in front of everyone. It means the consequences of ignoring wisdom become public and painful.
entries.5:15: Drink water from your own well rather than from someone else's. It means find your intimacy and satisfaction in your own marriage, not elsewhere.
entries.5:16: Don't let your springs and streams flow out into the streets for anyone to use. It means keep what is private and precious within your marriage.
entries.5:17: Let them belong to you alone and not be shared with other men. It means your intimate life is meant for you and your spouse only.
entries.5:18: Let your own fountain be blessed, and enjoy the wife you married when you were young. It means be grateful for and delight in your marriage.
entries.5:19: She is like a lovely deer; let her love satisfy you and delight you always. It means find ongoing joy and pleasure in your own wife.
entries.5:20: Why would you, my son, wander off with another woman and hold her in your arms? It means it makes no sense to leave your marriage for a temptation.
entries.5:21: The Lord sees everything a person does and weighs all their paths. It means nothing you do is hidden from God, and he judges it fairly.
entries.5:22: A wicked person gets trapped by his own wrongdoings, tied up by the cords of his sin. It means sin catches you and holds you captive.
entries.5:23: He comes to ruin because he refused instruction, and his great foolishness makes him wander off the right path. It means ignoring wisdom leads a person astray to their own harm.
entries.6:1: This warns that promising to pay someone else's debt makes you responsible for it. It means be careful before you take on someone else's obligations.
entries.6:2: Your own words have trapped you like an animal in a net. What you promised now holds you, so think before you speak.
entries.6:3: Since you are now in your neighbor's power, act quickly to get free. Go to him right away and humbly ask to be released from the promise.
entries.6:4: Don't put it off or rest until you have settled the matter. Deal with it before you sleep.
entries.6:5: Get yourself out of the trap as fast as a deer escapes a hunter or a bird escapes a net. Act quickly to free yourself.
entries.6:6: Watch how ants live and learn from them, especially if you tend to be lazy. Their example can teach you wisdom.
entries.6:7: Ants have no boss or leader telling them what to do. They work without being supervised.
entries.6:8: Ants gather and store food ahead of time for when it is needed. They plan ahead instead of waiting until trouble comes.
entries.6:9: This asks a lazy person how long they will keep sleeping and putting off work. It is a call to get up and act.
entries.6:10: A little more sleep and a little more rest, and you keep putting things off. Small excuses add up.
entries.6:11: Poverty will come on you suddenly like a robber or an armed attacker. Laziness brings loss before you realize it.
entries.6:12: A worthless, trouble-making person goes around telling lies. Their words cause harm wherever they go.
entries.6:13: They signal with their eyes, feet, and fingers to hint at secret plans. They scheme quietly instead of speaking honestly.
entries.6:14: Their mind is always planning evil and stirring up conflict. They enjoy causing trouble.
entries.6:15: Disaster will hit such a person suddenly, and no one will be able to help them. Their scheming ends in ruin.
entries.6:16: God hates certain behaviors, and the writer lists seven that disgust him. These are things he strongly opposes.
entries.6:17: God hates proud looks, lying words, and hands that kill innocent people. These actions are deeply wrong to him.
entries.6:18: God hates a heart that plans evil and feet that rush to do wrong. He sees the intentions behind the actions.
entries.6:19: God hates a witness who lies and someone who stirs up trouble among family and friends. Dishonesty and division are hateful to him.
entries.6:20: Listen to your father's instruction and don't forget what your mother taught you. Their guidance is worth keeping.
entries.6:21: Hold these teachings close in your heart and keep them always with you. Make them a constant part of your life.
entries.6:22: This teaching will guide you as you walk, watch over you as you sleep, and speak to you when you wake. Good instruction protects you all day long.
entries.6:23: Good rules and teaching are like a light showing you the right path. They lead you toward life.
entries.6:24: These teachings will keep you away from a seductive woman and her flattering words. Wisdom protects you from being led astray.
entries.6:25: Don't let your desires chase after her beauty or let her looks capture you. Guard your heart instead of being drawn in.
entries.6:26: A prostitute may cost you only money, but another man's wife can cost you your life. The danger is far greater than it looks.
entries.6:27: Can you hold fire against your chest without your clothes catching fire? No, and you can't get close to this sin without being hurt.
entries.6:28: Can you walk on hot coals without burning your feet? No, so you can't touch this sin and escape the damage.
entries.6:29: Anyone who sleeps with his neighbor's wife will not escape punishment. The consequences are certain.
entries.6:30: People don't despise a thief too much if he steals only because he is starving. There is some understanding for desperate need.
entries.6:31: Even so, a thief who is caught must pay back seven times over, giving up everything he owns. Stealing still carries a heavy cost.
entries.6:32: A man who takes another man's wife has lost his senses and is destroying himself. He is ruining his own life.
entries.6:33: He will get wounds and lose his honor, and his shame will not be erased. The damage cannot be undone.
entries.6:34: A jealous husband will be furious and show no mercy when he punishes. The betrayed man's anger will be fierce.
entries.6:35: No amount of money or gifts will settle the matter or make peace. The wrong cannot be bought off.
entries.7:1: The father urges his son to hold on to his teaching and store it safely in his mind. It means we should treat good advice as something valuable worth keeping close.
entries.7:2: Following wise instruction protects your life, and this teaching should be as precious to you as your own eyesight. It means wisdom helps you see clearly and stay safe.
entries.7:3: The teaching should be tied to your hands and written on your heart, so it shapes what you do and what you love. It means wisdom should be part of your everyday actions, not just something you hear.
entries.7:4: Treat wisdom like a close sister and make understanding your best friend. It means you should want wisdom the way you want the people you love most.
entries.7:5: This wisdom will guard you from a seductive woman whose smooth words can lead you astray. It means good judgment helps you spot and resist flattery that could harm you.
entries.7:6: The teacher describes looking out through his window and watching what happens on the street. It sets the scene for a real-life example he is about to tell.
entries.7:7: Among the people he saw a young man who lacked good sense. It means foolishness often shows up as a lack of careful thinking.
entries.7:8: The young man walked down the street near her corner, heading toward her house. It means he put himself in the path of temptation instead of staying away.
entries.7:9: It was evening, then dusk, then deep darkness of night. It means the setting made it easier to do something he would not want seen in daylight.
entries.7:10: The woman came out to meet him dressed to seduce, with a scheming heart. It means her appearance hid a plan to trap him.
entries.7:11: She is loud and out of control, never staying at home. It means her life is restless and disorderly, not steady or trustworthy.
entries.7:12: She is out in the streets and open squares, waiting at every corner. It means she is actively looking for someone to lure in.
entries.7:13: She grabbed him, kissed him, and spoke to him with no shame. It means she boldly pushed past normal boundaries to get what she wanted.
entries.7:14: She claims she has offered her peace offerings and kept her vows today. It means she uses religion as a cover, making wrong seem acceptable.
entries.7:15: She says she came out hoping to find him and now has him. It means her words are designed to make him feel special and wanted.
entries.7:16: She describes her bed with fine embroidered cushions and Egyptian linens. It means she uses luxury and comfort as bait.
entries.7:17: She has perfumed her bed with sweet-smelling spices. It means she appeals to the senses to make the trap more attractive.
entries.7:18: She invites him to enjoy love with her all night. It means she offers immediate pleasure while hiding the cost.
entries.7:19: She says her husband is away on a long trip. It means she uses the promise of secrecy to make him feel safe.
entries.7:20: She says he took money with him and will not return until the full moon. It means she gives a timeline so he thinks there is no risk of being caught.
entries.7:21: Her smooth, flattering words wore him down and persuaded him. It means sweet talk can overpower good sense if you keep listening.
entries.7:22: The foolish young man follows her like an ox being led to slaughter, or like a deer caught by a rope. It means he goes willingly without realizing he is heading for disaster.
entries.7:23: He is like a bird caught in a net, unaware his life is in danger until the arrow strikes. It means the harm comes suddenly, after it is too late to escape.
entries.7:24: The father now tells his sons to listen carefully to what he is saying. It means this warning is meant for everyone, not just the young man in the story.
entries.7:25: Do not let your heart turn toward her ways or wander down her path. It means guard your desires, because wanting the wrong thing is the first step toward doing it.
entries.7:26: Many have been wounded and brought down by her, and a huge number have died through her. It means the damage from this kind of temptation is widespread and serious.
entries.7:27: Her house leads down to the grave, to the rooms of death. It means going that way ends in ruin, not the pleasure it promises.
entries.8:1: Wisdom is pictured as a woman calling out loudly in public, not hiding. God's wisdom is available to everyone who will listen, including you.
entries.8:2: She stands where roads meet and on high places, the spots where people pass by. Wisdom is placed right where ordinary people can find it.
entries.8:3: She calls out at the town gates and doorways, the busiest places. Wisdom speaks where life actually happens, not only in quiet corners.
entries.8:4: Her call goes out to all people, men and women alike. No one is left out of the invitation to hear wisdom.
entries.8:5: People who are naive or foolish are told to learn good sense and take correction. It is worth admitting you lack understanding so you can grow.
entries.8:6: Her words are true and honest, and she speaks what is right. What wisdom says can be trusted, so listen carefully.
entries.8:7: Truth comes from her mouth, and lying is hateful to her. Wisdom and dishonesty cannot live together.
entries.8:8: Everything she says is right, with nothing crooked or misleading in it. You never have to second-guess honest wisdom.
entries.8:9: Her words are clear and fair to anyone paying attention and wanting to learn. Understanding comes to those who are willing to see.
entries.8:10: Choose her instruction over silver and knowledge over fine gold. What wisdom gives you is worth more than money.
entries.8:11: Wisdom is more valuable than jewels, and nothing you could wish for compares to her. Put wisdom first when you weigh what matters.
entries.8:12: Wisdom lives alongside good sense and is found with careful planning. Sound thinking and wise choices go together.
entries.8:13: Respecting the Lord means turning away from evil, including pride, arrogance, bad conduct, and lying. A right fear of God shows up in what you refuse to do.
entries.8:14: Good advice, sound judgment, understanding, and strength all belong to wisdom. Real strength comes with clear thinking.
entries.8:15: Kings rule and leaders make just laws through wisdom. Good authority depends on wisdom, not just power.
entries.8:16: Rulers and nobles govern rightly because of wisdom. Fair leadership is built on it.
entries.8:17: Wisdom loves those who love her, and those who search for her earnestly will find her. If you truly want wisdom, you will get it.
entries.8:18: Riches and honor, lasting wealth and right living, come with wisdom. What she offers is wealth that does not rot away.
entries.8:19: What wisdom produces is better than pure gold, and her gain is worth more than silver. Her rewards outshine money.
entries.8:20: She walks the path of right living and fair judgment. Wisdom stays on the straight road, not the crooked one.
entries.8:21: She gives lasting wealth to those who love her and fills their storehouses. Loving wisdom leads to real, lasting provision.
entries.8:22: The Lord created wisdom at the very beginning, the first of his works long ago. Wisdom is not a new idea but goes back to the start of everything.
entries.8:23: She was set in place from ages past, before the world began. Wisdom is older than creation itself.
entries.8:24: She existed before the oceans and springs of water were made. Wisdom was there before the deep waters came to be.
entries.8:25: She was born before the mountains and hills were set in place. Wisdom predates the great landmarks of the earth.
entries.8:26: She was there before the land, the fields, or the first dust of the world. Wisdom came before the ground you stand on.
entries.8:27: She was present when God set up the heavens and marked out the horizon over the deep. Wisdom watched creation take shape.
entries.8:28: She was there when God made the skies firm and fixed the springs of the deep. Wisdom saw the foundations of the world laid.
entries.8:29: She was there when God set limits on the sea and laid the earth's foundations. Wisdom witnessed the boundaries God gave creation.
entries.8:30: She was beside God like a skilled craftsman, bringing him delight day after day and rejoicing before him. Wisdom was God's joyful partner in making the world.
entries.8:31: She rejoiced in the whole earth, and her delight was in people. Wisdom takes pleasure in human beings and in the world God made.
entries.8:32: She now calls her listeners her children and says those who keep her ways are happy. Listening to wisdom is the path to a blessed life.
entries.8:33: Hear her instruction, become wise, and do not let it go. Hold on to wisdom once you have heard it.
entries.8:34: The person who listens to her, waiting daily at her doors, is happy. Patient, daily attention to wisdom brings blessing.
entries.8:35: Whoever finds wisdom finds life and receives favor from the Lord. Gaining wisdom is gaining what truly matters.
entries.8:36: Whoever rejects her harms his own soul, and those who hate her are choosing death. Turning away from wisdom hurts you most of all.
entries.9:1: Wisdom is pictured as a woman who builds a strong, complete house to welcome people into. It means wisdom prepares a good life for those who accept it, and you are invited to come in.
entries.9:2: She has prepared a full meal with meat and wine and set the table, ready for guests. This means wisdom offers something real and satisfying, not just words, and it is ready for you now.
entries.9:3: She sends her servants out to call everyone from the highest, most visible places in town. This means wisdom is not hidden or only for special people; its invitation reaches everyone, including you.
entries.9:4: She calls to people who are naive or lack understanding and invites them in. This means wisdom is for ordinary, imperfect people, so you don't need to be smart or good enough first.
entries.9:5: She urges them to eat her bread and drink her wine. This means wisdom wants you to actually take what it offers and make it part of your life, not just admire it from a distance.
entries.9:6: She tells the simple to leave their foolish ways and walk the path of understanding so they can truly live. This means growing wise requires leaving old habits behind, and that choice leads to real life for you.
entries.9:7: Correcting a proud person usually backfires and brings you shame or a bad reputation. This means it is wise to think about who you are correcting, because some people will only turn on you.
entries.9:8: Don't bother correcting a proud person, since they will resent you, but a wise person will appreciate it and value you. This means your correction does more good, and costs you less, when given to someone willing to listen.
entries.9:9: Teach a wise person and they grow wiser still; train a good person and they learn even more. This means wisdom keeps growing in people who are open to learning, so stay teachable yourself.
entries.9:10: Revering the Lord is where wisdom begins, and knowing the Holy One gives you understanding. This means real wisdom starts with taking God seriously, so let respect for God shape how you think and live.
entries.9:11: Wisdom promises that those who follow her will live longer, fuller lives. This means wise choices tend to protect and lengthen your life, so listening to wisdom pays off in your own days.
entries.9:12: If you are wise, you benefit yourself; if you are proud, you alone bear the harm. This means your choices about wisdom mostly affect you, so you can't blame anyone else for the outcome.
entries.9:13: The foolish woman is loud and reckless and understands nothing. This means foolishness is noisy and empty, so don't mistake loud confidence for real sense.
entries.9:14: She sits at the door of her house in the high places of the town. This means foolishness also makes itself easy to find, so you will meet its offers in everyday places.
entries.9:15: She calls out to people walking by, going straight on their way. This means foolishness targets ordinary people minding their own business, so watch out for temptation when you least expect it.
entries.9:16: She uses the same invitation as wisdom, calling to the naive and those without sense. This means foolishness can sound just like wisdom, so you need to look closely at what is really being offered.
entries.9:17: She says stolen water tastes sweet and secret food is pleasant. This means sin feels exciting partly because it is hidden and forbidden, so don't trust feelings alone to tell you what is good.
entries.9:18: Her guests don't realize that the dead are there and that her path leads down to the grave. This means the pleasure of foolishness hides its deadly end, so look past the thrill to where a choice will actually lead you.
entries.10:1: Good choices by a child bring joy to parents, while foolish choices bring grief. Your decisions affect the people who raised you.
entries.10:2: Money gained by doing wrong does not really help you, but living rightly saves you from ruin. Honesty matters more than profit.
entries.10:3: God cares for those who do right and does not leave them hungry, but he blocks the desires of those who do evil. You can trust God to provide when you live honestly.
entries.10:4: Laziness leads to poverty, while steady hard work brings income. Effort in your daily work pays off.
entries.10:5: Gathering your crops at harvest time is wise, but sleeping through it brings shame. Pay attention and work when the time is right.
entries.10:6: Good things come to those who do right, but trouble covers the faces of those who do wrong. Your conduct shapes what comes back to you.
entries.10:7: People remember good people with fondness, but the memory of the wicked fades away. Live so that people remember you well.
entries.10:8: A wise person accepts correction, but a fool who talks too much trips himself up. Be willing to listen rather than always speaking.
entries.10:9: People who live honestly walk safely, but those who take crooked paths get caught. Integrity keeps you out of trouble.
entries.10:10: Winking to signal deceit stirs up trouble, but openly pointing out someone's fault brings peace. Be straightforward rather than sneaky.
entries.10:11: The words of a good person give life, but the words of the wicked bring harm. What you say can help or hurt others.
entries.10:12: Hatred stirs up conflict, but love overlooks faults. Choosing love calms quarrels instead of fueling them.
entries.10:13: Wisdom shows in what a wise person says, but a person with no sense needs discipline. Let your words show understanding.
entries.10:14: Wise people hold on to knowledge, but a fool's mouth brings trouble quickly. Be careful not to blurt out everything you think.
entries.10:15: Wealth feels like a safe fortress to the rich, but poverty leaves the poor feeling helpless. Money can feel like security, though it is not the same as real safety.
entries.10:16: The earnings of a good person lead to life, but what the wicked gain leads to sin. Let your work produce good, not harm.
entries.10:17: Listening to correction keeps you on the path of life, but ignoring it leads others astray. Accept guidance when it comes.
entries.10:18: Hiding hatred behind kind words is wrong, and spreading rumors about others is foolish. Be honest and refuse to gossip.
entries.10:19: Talking too much leads to sin, but holding your tongue shows wisdom. Sometimes saying less is the wiser choice.
entries.10:20: The words of a good person are valuable like pure silver, but the heart of the wicked is worth little. Speak words that have real worth.
entries.10:21: Good people's words feed and help others, but fools starve for lack of sense. Use your words to nourish people around you.
entries.10:22: When God blesses you with wealth, it does not come with added sorrow, and hard work alone cannot match it. Receive good things with gratitude rather than anxiety.
entries.10:23: Fools treat doing wrong as a game, but sensible people enjoy wisdom. Take wrongdoing seriously instead of treating it as fun.
entries.10:24: What the wicked fear will catch up with them, but good people will get what they hope for. Your hopes and fears tend to shape what finds you.
entries.10:25: When the storm passes, the wicked are gone, but good people stand firm forever. Build your life on what lasts.
entries.10:26: A lazy worker frustrates those who send him, like vinegar on teeth or smoke in eyes. Do your part so you don't wear out the people who rely on you.
entries.10:27: Revering the Lord leads to a longer life, but the years of the wicked are cut short. Respecting God shapes how you live your days.
entries.10:28: Good people's hopes bring joy, but the wicked have nothing to look forward to. Put your hope in what will not disappoint.
entries.10:29: Following the Lord's way is a strong shelter for good people, but ruin for those who do evil. The same path protects some and exposes others.
entries.10:30: Good people will not be shaken, but the wicked will not stay settled in the land. Living rightly gives you lasting stability.
entries.10:31: A good person's words produce wisdom, but a lying tongue will be silenced. Let your speech grow something good.
entries.10:32: Good people know how to say what is helpful, but the wicked only speak what is crooked. Choose words that are kind and true.
entries.11:1: God hates dishonest business and cheating people with false measures, but he is pleased when we are honest and fair. So treat others fairly in every deal, because God sees how you weigh things.
entries.11:2: Pride leads to disgrace, while humility and a quiet spirit bring wisdom. If you think too highly of yourself, you will fall; staying humble keeps you wise.
entries.11:3: Honesty guides good people safely, but dishonesty ruins those who twist the truth. Let integrity be your guide, because crooked ways eventually destroy the person who walks in them.
entries.11:4: Money cannot save you when judgment comes, but living rightly keeps you safe from death. Do not trust your wealth to rescue you; trust God and live uprightly.
entries.11:5: A good person's honesty makes their path straight, but sin trips up the wicked. Live honestly and your way will be clearer; sin will make you stumble.
entries.11:6: Honesty saves the upright, but the treacherous are caught in their own schemes. Do what is right and you will be rescued, while evil plans trap the one who makes them.
entries.11:7: When a good person dies, their hope does not end, but the hope of the wicked dies with them. Put your hope in what lasts, because the hopes of the wicked come to nothing.
entries.11:8: The honest person is rescued from trouble, and the wicked one ends up in their place. God can bring you out of trouble, so keep doing what is right.
entries.11:9: A wicked person's words can destroy a neighbor, but knowledge rescues the honest. Be careful with your words, and let wisdom keep you from harm.
entries.11:10: When good people prosper, the whole town rejoices, and when the wicked die, people celebrate. A good person's success blesses the community around them.
entries.11:11: Honest people bring blessing that makes a town great, but the words of the wicked tear it down. Your integrity and speech affect the people around you.
entries.11:12: Looking down on your neighbor shows you lack sense, but a wise person keeps quiet. Do not despise others; wisdom often means holding your tongue.
entries.11:13: A gossip tells secrets, but a trustworthy person keeps them. Be someone who can be trusted with what others share.
entries.11:14: Without good advice a people fall, but with many wise counselors they are safe. Seek wise advice before making big decisions.
entries.11:15: Promising to pay for a stranger's debt brings trouble, but refusing such deals keeps you safe. Be careful about taking on risky obligations for people you do not know.
entries.11:16: A gracious woman receives honor, but a shameful one brings disgrace; those who hate work lose out, while the strong keep their wealth. Kindness brings honor, and hard work protects what you have.
entries.11:17: A kind person benefits themselves, but a cruel person brings trouble on themselves. Be merciful, because cruelty hurts you most of all.
entries.11:18: The wicked earn wages that deceive, but the one who plants righteousness gets a sure reward. Do good even when it is hard, because God's reward is certain.
entries.11:19: Living rightly leads to life, but chasing evil leads to death. Choose what is right, because it leads to life, while evil leads to ruin.
entries.11:20: God hates people with twisted hearts, but he delights in those who walk blamelessly. Keep your heart honest and your ways straight, because God takes pleasure in that.
entries.11:21: Evildoers will not escape punishment, but the children of the upright will be safe. Do what is right, because God's justice is certain and he protects the families of the honest.
entries.11:22: A beautiful woman without good sense is like a gold ring in a pig's snout. Beauty without wisdom is wasted and out of place, so value good sense above looks.
entries.11:23: Good people desire only good things, but what the wicked expect is wrath. Let your desires aim at what is good, because evil brings only trouble.
entries.11:24: One person gives freely and grows richer, while another hoards too much and ends up in need. Be generous, because holding back too tightly can leave you empty.
entries.11:25: Those who bless others will be blessed and satisfied, but those who curse will be cursed. Be generous with your kindness, because it comes back to you.
entries.11:26: People curse the one who hoards grain, but they bless the one who sells it fairly. Do not profit from others' need; share what you have and be blessed.
entries.11:27: Whoever eagerly seeks good finds favor, but whoever looks for trouble will get it. Aim at what is good, because you tend to find what you go looking for.
entries.11:28: Trusting in riches leads to ruin, but the upright flourish like a green leaf. Do not put your confidence in money; trust God and you will thrive.
entries.11:29: Whoever brings trouble on their own household inherits nothing but wind, and the fool ends up serving the wise. Do not wreck your home with foolishness, because folly leads to loss and servitude.
entries.11:30: Righteousness is like a tree of life, but violence destroys lives. Live rightly and you will bring life to others, while violence only takes life away.
entries.11:31: If good people are rewarded on earth, how much more will the wicked and sinful be punished. God is just, so do not envy sinners; everyone will answer for how they live.
entries.12:1: Being willing to learn and accept correction is how you gain real knowledge. If you hate being taught, you stay foolish and miss out on what would help you grow.
entries.12:2: God looks kindly on a good person, but he opposes those who plan to do harm. Your character and intentions matter to God, so aim to be genuinely good.
entries.12:3: Doing wrong may feel like it protects you, but it never makes you truly safe. Honest people may be shaken, yet their foundation holds firm.
entries.12:4: A good, faithful wife brings honor and strength to her husband, while a wife who brings shame wears him down. The character of a spouse deeply affects the other person's life.
entries.12:5: Good people plan things that are fair and right, but those who do evil plan ways to deceive others. Check whether your plans are honest or whether they rely on tricking people.
entries.12:6: Wicked people use words to tear others down and destroy them, but honest people use their words to rescue and protect. Your words can either harm someone or help them, so choose carefully.
entries.12:7: Those who do evil are eventually swept away, but honest people and what they build last. Living uprightly gives you something that endures.
entries.12:8: People respect and praise someone who shows good sense, but a person with twisted thinking is looked down on. Wisdom earns respect, while foolishness loses it.
entries.12:9: It is better to be humble and have enough, even with help, than to act important while going hungry. Don't chase appearances at the cost of real needs.
entries.12:10: A good person cares about the well-being of their animals, but cruel people are hard-hearted even toward creatures that depend on them. How you treat animals shows something about your heart.
entries.12:11: Hard work on your own land or job brings steady food and security, but chasing after worthless people and schemes leaves you with nothing. Put your effort into real, productive work.
entries.12:12: What wicked people build on will collapse, but the foundation of honest people lasts forever. Invest your life in what is right, because it endures.
entries.12:13: People who sin with their words get trapped by their own lies, but an honest person escapes trouble. Watch your words, because careless or dishonest speech can catch you.
entries.12:14: Good words and honest work both bring rewards. What you say and what you do will come back to you as benefit.
entries.12:15: A foolish person thinks their own way is always right, but a wise person listens to advice. Be willing to hear others, because you don't always see your own mistakes.
entries.12:16: A fool shows their anger right away, but a sensible person holds back and covers over an insult. Controlling your temper and not reacting instantly shows maturity.
entries.12:17: An honest witness tells the truth and helps people see what is right, but a false witness spreads lies. Tell the truth, because lies hurt others and distort what is fair.
entries.12:18: Reckless words cut people like a sword, but wise words bring healing. Your words have real power to wound or to mend, so use them to heal.
entries.12:19: Truthful words stand the test of time, but lies are soon exposed and gone. Build your life on truth, because it lasts while deception does not.
entries.12:20: People who plan evil carry deceit in their hearts, but those who work for peace find joy. Aim for peace with others, because that path leads to happiness.
entries.12:21: Honest people are not overwhelmed by trouble, but those who do evil end up full of it. Living rightly protects you from much of the harm that wrongdoing brings.
entries.12:22: God hates lying lips but delights in people who are truthful and faithful. Be honest, because truthfulness pleases God.
entries.12:23: A wise person doesn't show off everything they know, but a fool blurts out their foolishness for all to see. Knowing when to stay quiet is a mark of wisdom.
entries.12:24: People who work hard and are diligent end up in charge, while those who are lazy end up doing forced labor. Effort and reliability lead to a better position in life.
entries.12:25: Worry weighs a person down, but a kind word lifts their spirits. A simple encouraging word can make a real difference to someone who is anxious.
entries.12:26: A good person points their neighbor in the right direction, but the path of evildoers leads people astray. Your example influences others, so lead them toward what is right.
entries.12:27: A lazy person doesn't even go after the food they need, but a diligent worker gains wealth. Being willing to put in effort is what brings you what you need.
entries.12:28: The path of doing right leads to life, but the way of evil leads to death. Choose to live rightly, because that path leads to life rather than ruin.
entries.13:1: A wise person welcomes correction and learns from it, while someone who resists authority refuses to listen even when spoken to sharply. It means you should stay teachable, because refusing advice keeps you stuck.
entries.13:2: What you say comes back to you: good words bring good results, but people who want what is wrong end up chasing violence. Watch what you want, because it shapes what you do.
entries.13:3: Being careful about what you say protects your life, but talking too much without restraint leads to trouble. It means guarding your words is a way of protecting yourself.
entries.13:4: A lazy person never gets what he longs for, while those who work hard get plenty. It means wanting something isn't enough; effort is what brings it about.
entries.13:5: Honest people hate lies, but a wrongdoer earns a bad reputation and shame. It means your honesty or dishonesty shapes how people see you.
entries.13:6: Living rightly keeps a person safe, but sin brings the wicked down. It means doing what is right protects you, while doing wrong eventually ruins you.
entries.13:7: Someone can pretend to be rich and have nothing, while another looks poor but has great wealth. It means appearances can fool you, so don't judge people by how they seem.
entries.13:8: A rich person may have to pay out his wealth to save his life, while a poor person isn't bothered by such threats. It means wealth brings its own dangers, and having little can sometimes be safer.
entries.13:9: Life shines brightly for good people, but the light of those who do wrong goes out. It means honesty brings hope and a future, while wrongdoing ends in darkness.
entries.13:10: Pride only stirs up quarrels, but people who are humble and calm have wisdom. It means letting go of pride keeps peace, while insisting on your own way starts fights.
entries.13:11: Money gained quickly slips away, but wealth built up by steady work grows. It means slow, honest effort pays off more than get-rich-quick schemes.
entries.13:12: Hope that keeps being delayed makes the heart sick, but getting what you long for brings fresh life. It means waiting can be painful, and fulfilled hope is deeply refreshing.
entries.13:13: Someone who mocks instruction will be ruined, but whoever respects the law is rewarded. It means taking good teaching seriously pays off, while sneering at it hurts you.
entries.13:14: The teaching of wise people is like a life-giving spring that turns you away from deadly traps. It means good advice can save you from serious harm.
entries.13:15: Good sense earns people's favor, but the way of the treacherous leads to ruin. It means acting wisely wins respect, while dishonesty destroys you.
entries.13:16: A sensible person acts with knowledge, but a fool shows off his foolishness for all to see. It means thinking before you act, rather than letting everyone see your mistakes.
entries.13:17: A messenger who spreads false reports causes trouble, but a faithful messenger brings healing. It means being reliable with what you pass on helps people, while lies hurt them.
entries.13:18: Ignoring correction brings poverty and shame, but accepting instruction brings honor. It means listening when you're corrected leads to a better life.
entries.13:19: Getting what you deeply desire is sweet, but fools find it disgusting to turn away from evil. It means good things satisfy, yet foolish people resist giving up what harms them.
entries.13:20: Spending time with wise people makes you wise, but keeping company with fools brings harm. It means your friends shape who you become, so choose them carefully.
entries.13:21: Trouble chases after sinners, but good things come to those who do right. It means your choices tend to bring matching results into your life.
entries.13:22: A good person leaves an inheritance for grandchildren, while a sinner's wealth ends up with the righteous. It means doing good builds something that lasts beyond you.
entries.13:23: Poor people's land can produce plenty of food, but injustice sweeps it away. It means there is often enough to go around, yet unfairness leaves people hungry.
entries.13:24: A parent who never disciplines his child is not being kind, but a loving parent corrects with care. It means loving your children includes guiding them, not just letting them do as they please.
entries.13:25: Good people have enough to eat, but the wicked go hungry. It means living rightly tends to bring satisfaction, while wrongdoing leaves you empty.
entries.14:1: A wise woman builds up her home, while a foolish one tears it down by her own actions. What you do and say each day either strengthens your household or damages it.
entries.14:2: People who live honestly show respect for God, but those who take crooked paths show they don't honor him. Your everyday choices reveal what you really think of God.
entries.14:3: A foolish person's own words get them into trouble, like a stick that hits their own back, while wise words keep a person out of harm. Watch what you say, because your words can hurt you or protect you.
entries.14:4: An empty barn stays clean because there are no animals, but it's the hard work of the ox that brings a big harvest. Real profit comes from work that makes a mess, not from keeping everything tidy and doing nothing.
entries.14:5: A truthful witness says what is true, but a false witness pours out lies. Be someone whose word can be trusted, because lying hurts the people who depend on you.
entries.14:6: A person who scorns correction can search for wisdom and never find it, but understanding comes easily to those willing to learn. If you want to grow wise, stay humble and open to being taught.
entries.14:7: Stay away from a foolish person, because you won't learn anything worthwhile from them. Choose your companions carefully, since the people around you shape what you know.
entries.14:8: A sensible person's wisdom helps them see clearly which way to go, but a fool's own cleverness just leads them astray. Think carefully about your path instead of trusting whatever seems smart in the moment.
entries.14:9: People who reject what's right end up in wrong, but those who live uprightly find goodwill and grace. Doing right brings peace, while resisting it brings trouble.
entries.14:10: Only you truly know your own grief, and an outsider can't fully share your joy. Be gentle with people, because everyone carries hidden feelings you can't see.
entries.14:11: The home of a wicked person will come down, but the tent of an honest person will stand and flourish. Living rightly builds something lasting, even if it looks modest.
entries.14:12: A path can look right to you and still lead to death in the end. Don't trust your own sense of direction without checking where it's really taking you.
entries.14:13: A person can laugh while their heart is sad, and joy can be followed by grief. Don't assume a smiling face means everything is fine, and don't expect happiness to last forever.
entries.14:14: A person who turns away from God will get exactly what their ways deserve, and a good person will be rewarded for what they do. Your choices will come back to you in full.
entries.14:15: A naive person believes everything they hear, but a sensible person thinks about each step they take. Check things out before you trust them or act on them.
entries.14:16: A wise person is careful and turns away from evil, but a fool rushes ahead in pride without noticing the danger. Being cautious isn't weakness; it's wisdom.
entries.14:17: Someone quick to get angry does foolish things, but a sensible person stays calm. Slow down when you're upset, because anger makes people act badly.
entries.14:18: Foolish people end up with foolishness as their inheritance, while sensible people gain knowledge like a crown. What you pursue now is what you'll end up with.
entries.14:19: In the end, evil people will bow low before good people, and wrongdoers will end up at the doors of those who live rightly. Doing right may seem hard now, but it wins in the end.
entries.14:20: A poor person is avoided even by their neighbor, but a rich person has plenty of friends. People often treat you based on what you have, so don't mistake that for real friendship.
entries.14:21: Looking down on your neighbor is wrong, but whoever is kind to the poor is truly happy. Treating people with kindness, especially those with little, brings real joy.
entries.14:22: People who plan evil will go wrong, but those who plan good find mercy and faithfulness. What you set your heart on planning shapes what you receive.
entries.14:23: Hard work in anything brings profit, but mere talk only leads to poverty. Doing something, even imperfectly, beats only talking about it.
entries.14:24: Wisdom is like a crown for the wise, but foolishness is all a fool has to show. What you build up in your mind is what people will see in your life.
entries.14:25: A truthful witness saves lives, but a liar spreads deceit and harm. Telling the truth can protect people, while lying puts them in danger.
entries.14:26: Whoever deeply respects the Lord has strong confidence, and their children have a safe place to turn. Trusting God gives you and your family real security.
entries.14:27: Respecting the Lord is like a spring of life that keeps you away from deadly traps. Taking God seriously helps you avoid the things that would ruin you.
entries.14:28: A king's honor comes from having many people, and a ruler with no people is ruined. Leaders depend on the people they lead, so their worth isn't measured by power alone.
entries.14:29: Being slow to get angry shows great understanding, but a hot-tempered person just makes foolishness worse. Patience is a sign of real wisdom.
entries.14:30: A calm heart gives life to the body, but envy eats away at you like a disease in your bones. Peace of mind is healthy, while jealousy slowly destroys you.
entries.14:31: Treating the poor badly insults the God who made them, but being kind to those in need honors him. How you treat poor people shows what you think of their Maker.
entries.14:32: A wicked person is brought down by their own evil, but an honest person has hope even in death. Living rightly gives you hope that holds up to the end.
entries.14:33: Wisdom rests in the mind of a wise person, but it isn't found among fools. Wisdom lives in people who make room for it, not in those who reject it.
entries.14:34: A nation is lifted up by doing what is right, but sin brings shame to any people. Doing right makes a country strong, while wrong doing drags it down.
entries.14:35: A king is pleased with a servant who acts wisely, but he is angry with one who brings shame. Doing your work well earns favor, while careless failure brings trouble.
entries.15:1: A gentle reply calms someone's anger, while harsh words make things worse. Watch how you speak when someone is upset, because your tone can either cool things down or start a fight.
entries.15:2: Wise people use their words to share what they know, but fools just pour out nonsense. Aim to make your speech useful rather than just filling the air.
entries.15:3: God sees everything that happens everywhere, both good and evil. Nothing you do is hidden from him, so live honestly.
entries.15:4: Kind, healing words give life to people, but deceitful words crush a person's spirit. Choose words that build others up instead of tearing them down.
entries.15:5: A fool ignores the guidance his father gave him, but someone who accepts correction shows good sense. Be willing to learn from those who have taught you.
entries.15:6: An honest person's home holds real treasure, but money gained by wrongdoing brings trouble. Value integrity over dishonest gain.
entries.15:7: Wise people's words pass on real knowledge, but a fool's heart is not honest. Let what you say come from a heart that is right.
entries.15:8: God rejects the offerings of wicked people but delights in the prayers of those who do right. What matters to God is the character behind what you bring him.
entries.15:9: God hates the path of evildoers but loves those who pursue what is right. Make doing right your aim, not just appearing religious.
entries.15:10: Severe correction awaits someone who leaves the right path, and rejecting instruction leads to ruin. Accept discipline now rather than face worse later.
entries.15:11: God sees even the realm of the dead, so he certainly sees what is in human hearts. Live knowing that nothing in you is hidden from him.
entries.15:12: Someone who resents correction won't accept instruction and avoids wise people. Don't shut out the people who could help you grow.
entries.15:13: A happy heart shows on your face, but inner sorrow wears a person down. Pay attention to what is going on inside you and others.
entries.15:14: A sensible person hungers to learn, while foolish people feed on foolishness. Choose what you take in, because it shapes who you become.
entries.15:15: Someone weighed down by trouble sees every day as bad, but a cheerful heart enjoys life like a constant feast. Your outlook shapes how you experience your days.
entries.15:16: A little with reverence for God is better than great wealth mixed with trouble. Don't trade peace with God for more stuff.
entries.15:17: A simple meal shared with love beats a fancy dinner served with hatred. Relationships matter more than what is on the table.
entries.15:18: A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but someone slow to anger calms a quarrel. Being patient can stop a fight before it starts.
entries.15:19: A lazy person's path is full of obstacles, but the way of the diligent is clear. Hard work makes life's road smoother.
entries.15:20: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man treats his mother with contempt. Let your choices bring honor to your parents.
entries.15:21: Foolishness entertains the senseless, but a person with good sense walks a straight path. Don't let silly things steer your life.
entries.15:22: Plans fail without good advice, but they succeed when many wise people guide them. Ask for counsel before you commit to big decisions.
entries.15:23: A good answer brings a person joy, and a timely word is a wonderful thing. Speak up when your words can help someone at the right moment.
entries.15:24: Wisdom leads a person along the path of life and away from death. Let good sense guide your choices.
entries.15:25: The Lord tears down the proud person's house but protects the widow's property. God opposes arrogance and defends the vulnerable.
entries.15:26: God detests evil schemes but is pleased with words that are pure. Keep your thoughts and speech clean.
entries.15:27: Someone greedy for profit brings trouble on his own family, but a person who refuses bribes will live. Don't let money ruin the people closest to you.
entries.15:28: A righteous person thinks before answering, but a wicked person blurts out evil. Pause and consider your words before you speak.
entries.15:29: The Lord stays far from the wicked but listens to the prayers of those who do right. Live rightly and know that God hears you.
entries.15:30: Bright eyes and good news cheer a person up and even refresh the body. Good news and a hopeful look can lift someone's whole spirit.
entries.15:31: Anyone who listens to helpful correction will end up among the wise. Take good advice seriously and let it change you.
entries.15:32: Ignoring discipline means harming yourself, but listening to correction helps you gain wisdom. Accept being corrected; it's for your own good.
entries.15:33: Reverence for the Lord teaches wisdom, and humility comes before honor. Stay humble if you want to be lifted up.
entries.16:1: You can plan what you want to say, but the words that actually come out are guided by God. So make your plans, yet stay humble and let God shape the outcome.
entries.16:2: We tend to think everything we do is fine, but God weighs our real motives. Ask God to show you where your heart is not honest, because he sees what you cannot.
entries.16:3: Commit the work to God before you plan the outcome. He is the one who makes plans stand.
entries.16:4: God made everything with a purpose, and even evil people and hard days serve his larger plan. Nothing in your life is outside God's control, even the difficult parts.
entries.16:5: God deeply dislikes pride and will not let it go unpunished. Watch your heart for arrogance, because it puts you against God.
entries.16:6: Kindness, faithfulness, and a healthy fear of God turn a person away from doing wrong. Practice mercy and honesty, and let respect for God keep you from evil.
entries.16:7: When your life pleases God, he can even calm the people who are against you. Focus on living rightly and trust God to handle your enemies.
entries.16:8: A small amount gained honestly is better than a large amount gained by cheating. Be content with less if it means keeping your integrity.
entries.16:9: You can plan your path, but God is the one who actually directs your steps. Make your plans, but hold them loosely and let God lead.
entries.16:10: A king is expected to speak decisions that are right and fair. Those in authority should judge carefully, and the rest of us should value fair leadership.
entries.16:11: Honest scales and weights matter to God; fair dealing in business is his concern. Be fair and honest in every transaction, because God cares about how you treat others.
entries.16:12: Kings should hate evil because a ruler's authority rests on doing right. Leaders must be just, and we should support fairness in those who govern.
entries.16:13: Kings value people who speak honestly and rightly. Be a person whose words are truthful, because honesty is respected by good leaders.
entries.16:14: A king's anger can be deadly, but a wise person knows how to calm it. Stay calm and thoughtful when someone in power is angry, and work for peace.
entries.16:15: A king's favor brings life and blessing, like refreshing spring rain. It is good to seek the approval of those in authority by doing what is right.
entries.16:16: Wisdom and understanding are worth far more than money. Spend your effort gaining wisdom, because it is more valuable than any wealth.
entries.16:17: People who do right turn away from evil and guard their own lives. Watch your path carefully and avoid what is wrong, because that protects you.
entries.16:18: Pride comes before a fall, and a stubborn attitude leads to ruin. Stay humble, because thinking too highly of yourself sets you up for disaster.
entries.16:19: It is better to be humble and lowly than to share in the spoils of proud, violent people. Choose humility over the rewards that come from arrogance and conflict.
entries.16:20: Paying attention to good teaching brings benefit, and trusting God brings happiness. Listen to wise instruction and put your trust in the Lord.
entries.16:21: People with wisdom are known for good sense, and kind words help others learn. Speak graciously, because pleasant words make your wisdom easier to receive.
entries.16:22: Wisdom gives life to the one who has it, but foolishness brings its own punishment. Pursue wisdom, because it is life to you, while folly only hurts you.
entries.16:23: A wise person's heart guides what they say and helps them teach others well. Fill your heart with wisdom, and your words will follow.
entries.16:24: Kind words are sweet and healing, like honey to the soul and body. Speak gently to others, because gracious words bring health and life.
entries.16:25: A path can look right to us but still lead to death. Do not trust your own sense of direction alone; check your way against God's wisdom.
entries.16:26: A worker's hunger drives him to keep working, and that desire is useful. Honest need and effort are good motivations, so work diligently for what you need.
entries.16:27: A worthless person plans evil, and their words spread harm like fire. Avoid people who stir up trouble, and do not let your own words burn others.
entries.16:28: Twisted people cause conflict, and secret gossip breaks friendships apart. Do not spread rumors or stir up trouble, because it destroys relationships.
entries.16:29: A violent person pulls others into evil and leads them down a bad path. Be careful who influences you, and do not follow someone who encourages wrongdoing.
entries.16:30: Someone who hides their intentions and keeps quiet about evil is plotting trouble. Do not mistake silence for innocence; watch for schemes and stay away from them.
entries.16:31: Gray hair is a crown of honor when a person has lived rightly. Respect older people, and aim to live a long life of integrity.
entries.16:32: Being slow to anger and self-controlled is greater than winning battles. Work on patience and control of your temper, because that is true strength.
entries.16:33: People may cast lots to decide something, but the outcome is really from God. You can make decisions, but trust that God is the one who determines the result.
entries.17:1: A simple meal in a peaceful home is better than a big feast in a house full of fighting. It means you should value peace over plenty, because a calm home is worth more than wealth with conflict.
entries.17:2: A wise, faithful servant can end up leading a shameful son and sharing the family inheritance. It means that good character and hard work can be rewarded above family status.
entries.17:3: Fire tests and purifies silver and gold, and God tests people's hearts the same way. It means God sees what is really inside you, so let hard times refine your heart rather than harden it.
entries.17:4: People who do wrong listen to evil talk, and liars pay attention to harmful gossip. It means the words you choose to listen to show what kind of person you are, so guard your ears.
entries.17:5: Mocking the poor insults God who made them, and enjoying someone's trouble will not go unpunished. It means treat the poor with respect and never take pleasure in others' misfortune.
entries.17:6: Grandchildren are a joy and honor to the elderly, and children take pride in their parents. It means family generations are a gift to each other, so cherish the bonds between old and young.
entries.17:7: Fine, honest speech doesn't suit a fool, and even less do lies suit a ruler. It means people in positions of power especially should speak truthfully, because lies from leaders do great damage.
entries.17:8: A bribe looks like a precious stone to the one who has it, and he thinks it will make everything go his way. It means money can seem to open doors, but this is a warning about trusting in bribes rather than doing right.
entries.17:9: Overlooking someone's fault builds love, but repeating the matter over and over splits friends apart. It means forgive and let go of offenses instead of gossiping about them.
entries.17:10: A single correction reaches a wise person more deeply than a hundred beatings reach a fool. It means be quick to learn from a rebuke, because wisdom responds to words rather than needing force.
entries.17:11: A rebellious person is only out for trouble, so harsh punishment will be sent against him. It means refusing to be corrected leads to serious consequences, so stay teachable.
entries.17:12: Meeting an angry mother bear robbed of her cubs is safer than meeting a fool in the middle of foolishness. It means avoid foolish people when they are acting out, because their recklessness is dangerous.
entries.17:13: If someone repays good with evil, trouble will never leave his household. It means never return kindness with harm, because doing so brings lasting damage on yourself.
entries.17:14: A quarrel starts like a small leak in a dam, so stop it before it bursts into a fight. It means deal with conflict early and quietly, before it grows out of control.
entries.17:15: God detests both the person who lets the guilty go free and the one who punishes the innocent. It means fairness matters to God, so judge situations honestly and don't twist justice.
entries.17:16: It's pointless for a fool to hold money to buy wisdom when he has no desire to understand. It means wisdom can't be bought; it comes from wanting to learn, so cultivate a teachable heart.
entries.17:17: A true friend loves you at all times and stands by you like family when trouble comes. It means value loyal friends and be that kind of friend to others, especially in hard times.
entries.17:18: A person with no sense shakes hands on a deal and becomes responsible for a neighbor's debt. It means be careful about promising to pay someone else's debts, because it can cost you dearly.
entries.17:19: Whoever loves quarreling loves sin, and whoever builds a showy, proud entrance is asking for ruin. It means avoid picking fights and don't let pride lead you into destruction.
