entries.17:20: Nothing good comes to a person whose heart is set on evil, and a deceitful tongue brings trouble. It means what you plan and how you speak will shape your outcome, so choose honesty.
entries.17:21: A foolish son brings grief to his father and no joy to his parent. It means children's choices deeply affect their parents, so raise them with care and pray for their wisdom.
entries.17:22: A cheerful heart is good medicine for the body, but a broken spirit drains your strength. It means take care of your inner joy and encourage others, because attitude affects health.
entries.17:23: A wicked person takes a bribe from his pocket to twist a court decision. It means bribery corrupts justice, so refuse to let money sway what is right.
entries.17:24: A wise person keeps wisdom in view, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth. It means stay focused on what is wise and near rather than chasing every distraction.
entries.17:25: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitter pain to his mother. It means children's foolish choices hurt parents deeply, so honor your parents by living wisely.
entries.17:26: It is wrong to punish an innocent person or to beat honest leaders for doing right. It means never treat good people as if they were guilty, because justice should protect the upright.
entries.17:27: A person with knowledge speaks few words, and a calm spirit shows good sense. It means talk less and stay calm, because restraint is a mark of wisdom.
entries.17:28: Even a fool seems wise when he keeps quiet and holds his tongue. It means sometimes silence is the wisest thing you can do, so don't feel you must speak.
entries.18:1: Someone who cuts himself off from others to chase his own selfish plans is acting against good sense. It means isolating yourself for your own agenda usually ends badly, so stay connected to people who can guide you.
entries.18:2: A foolish person doesn't care about understanding; he just wants to blurt out whatever he's thinking. It's a warning to value listening and learning over simply voicing your own opinions.
entries.18:3: When wickedness shows up, contempt comes with it, and dishonor brings shame along too. It means the wrong you do and the disrespect you show end up dragging shame onto you.
entries.18:4: A person's words can be deep and full of meaning, and real wisdom flows out like a fresh stream. It means your speech can either be deep and life-giving or shallow, so aim for words that refresh others.
entries.18:5: It's wrong to favor the guilty or to rule against someone who is in the right. It means fairness matters, and you shouldn't bend justice just because you like or dislike someone.
entries.18:6: A fool's words start arguments, and his mouth gets him into trouble and even into fights. It means careless talk invites conflict, so watch what you say before it costs you.
entries.18:7: A fool's mouth ruins him, and his own words trap him. It means the things you say can become a snare that catches you, so speak with care.
entries.18:8: Gossip about a neighbor behind his back tastes sweet and sinks deep into the person who hears it. It means rumors are tempting to listen to but they lodge inside you and do real damage, so don't feed on them.
entries.18:9: Someone who is lazy about his work is a close relative of the one who destroys things. It means neglecting your responsibilities does as much harm as actively wrecking something, so do your work well.
entries.18:10: God's name is a place to run into, not a word to throw around. Safety is a person.
entries.18:11: A rich person's wealth feels like a fortified city and a high wall in his own mind. It means money can give a false sense of total safety, so don't trust your riches to protect you completely.
entries.18:12: Pride comes before a fall, but humility comes before honor. It means if you're full of yourself you're heading for trouble, while a humble attitude is the path to being respected.
entries.18:13: Answering before you've heard the whole matter is foolish and embarrassing. It means listen fully first, because jumping to reply makes you look bad and gets things wrong.
entries.18:14: A person's inner spirit can carry him through sickness, but if that spirit is crushed, what can lift him? It means your attitude and inner strength matter hugely in hard times, so guard your hope and encourage others whose spirit is broken.
entries.18:15: A sensible person's mind gains knowledge, and a wise person listens eagerly to learn more. It means keep your ears open and stay hungry to understand, because that's how wisdom grows.
entries.18:16: A gift opens doors for a person and brings him before important people. It means generosity can create opportunities and gain you access, so give wisely and kindly.
entries.18:17: The first person to present his case seems right until someone else comes and questions it. It means don't decide a matter after hearing only one side, because the full story often changes things.
entries.18:18: Casting lots settles disputes and separates strong opponents. It means sometimes a fair, neutral decision is needed to end a stalemate, so don't let arguments drag on endlessly.
entries.18:19: An offended brother is as hard to win back as a fortified city, and quarrels are like a barred tower. It means broken relationships are very hard to repair, so guard your close bonds and settle conflicts early.
entries.18:20: A person is filled by what his words produce, and he gets back the results of what he says. It means your words have consequences that come back to you, so speak in a way that brings good results.
entries.18:21: The tongue can bring death or life, and those who love to talk will eat the fruit of what they say. It means your words are powerful enough to help or harm, so choose them carefully.
entries.18:22: A man who finds a wife finds something good and receives favor from the Lord. It means a good marriage is a genuine blessing to be grateful for and to treat with care.
entries.18:23: A poor man pleads for mercy, but a rich man answers harshly. It means money can make people cold and rude, so be kind and generous rather than hard-hearted toward those in need.
entries.18:24: Some friends can ruin you, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother. It means choose your friends wisely, and value the rare friend who stays loyal through everything.
entries.19:1: It is better to be poor and honest than rich and dishonest. What matters most is how you live, not what you own.
entries.19:2: Wanting something badly without knowing what is right is dangerous, and rushing into action leads you off track. Think and learn before you act.
entries.19:3: People ruin their own lives by acting foolishly, and then they blame God for how things turned out. Take responsibility instead of getting angry at God.
entries.19:4: Money attracts plenty of friends, but a poor person loses even the friends he has. Notice who stays with you when you have nothing to offer.
entries.19:5: Someone who lies in court or spreads deceit will not escape punishment. Dishonesty catches up with you in the end.
entries.19:6: Many people try to win favor with a ruler, and everyone wants to be friends with someone who gives gifts. Be aware that some friendships are only about what they can get.
entries.19:7: When you are poor, even your own family turns against you, and your friends avoid you even more. Hardship shows who really cares.
entries.19:8: Gaining wisdom is a way of caring for yourself, and keeping good sense will bring you real good. Invest in understanding, because it pays off.
entries.19:9: A person who lies in court or speaks deceit will be punished and cut off. Lies eventually cost you everything.
entries.19:10: It is not fitting for a fool to live in luxury, and it is even worse for a servant to rule over princes. Comfort and power in the wrong hands cause trouble.
entries.19:11: Good sense makes a person slow to get angry, and overlooking an offense is to your credit. Patience and forgiveness are marks of strength.
entries.19:12: A king's anger is as frightening as a lion's roar, but his favor is as refreshing as dew on the grass. Treat those in authority with respect.
entries.19:13: A foolish son ruins his father, and a quarreling wife is like endless dripping rain. Foolishness and constant conflict wear a family down.
entries.19:14: Houses and money can be passed down from parents, but a sensible wife is a gift from the Lord. Value good character over inherited wealth.
entries.19:15: Laziness makes a person sleep his life away, and those who refuse to work will go hungry. Effort is necessary for getting what you need.
entries.19:16: Following the law keeps your life safe, but ignoring what you are told leads to death. Pay attention to instruction, because it protects you.
entries.19:17: Being kind to the poor is like lending to the Lord, and he will repay you. Generosity to those in need is never wasted.
entries.19:18: Discipline your child while there is still time to shape him, and don't let your anger go so far as to destroy him. Correct your children early, but with care.
entries.19:19: A person who flies into rages will keep paying for it, because if you rescue him once, you will have to do it again. Don't keep bailing out someone who won't change.
entries.19:20: Listen to advice and accept instruction, so that you will be wise in the end. Being teachable now pays off later.
entries.19:21: You may make many plans, but the Lord's purpose is the one that stands. Hold your plans loosely and trust God's direction.
entries.19:22: What makes a person attractive is kindness, and it is better to be poor than to be a liar. Character matters more than wealth.
entries.19:23: Revering the Lord leads to life, and those who do will be satisfied and kept from harm. A right attitude toward God brings real security.
entries.19:24: A lazy person buries his hand in the dish but won't even lift it to his mouth. Laziness can get so bad that a person won't even help himself.
entries.19:25: When a proud person is punished, the naive learn a lesson, and a sharp warning makes a wise person wiser. Learn from the correction of others.
entries.19:26: A son who mistreats his father and drives away his mother brings shame and disgrace. Treating your parents badly dishonors you too.
entries.19:27: If a son stops listening to instruction, he turns away from words that would make him wise. Keep listening to good teaching, or you will drift from it.
entries.19:28: A worthless witness mocks justice, and the mouths of wicked people pour out evil. Don't be part of dishonesty or gossip.
entries.19:29: Punishment is ready for the proud, and beatings are prepared for the back of fools. Pride and foolishness bring their own consequences.
entries.20:1: Alcohol makes people act foolishly and get into fights, so anyone who is led astray by drink is not being wise. Be careful with alcohol, because it can take away your good judgment.
entries.20:2: A king's anger is as dangerous as a lion's roar, so anyone who provokes him is only hurting himself. Treat people in authority with respect, because picking a fight with them costs you.
entries.20:3: It is a credit to a person to stay out of arguments, while fools are always ready to quarrel. Choosing peace over fighting makes you look good, not weak.
entries.20:4: A lazy person won't work when it's cold, so when harvest time comes he has nothing and begs in vain. If you put off work now, you will go without later.
entries.20:5: A person's real plans are hidden deep like water in a well, but someone with understanding knows how to draw them out. Wise people listen and ask questions to understand what others really think.
entries.20:6: Many people claim to be loyal and kind, but a truly faithful person is hard to find. It is easy to talk about being reliable; actually being reliable is what counts.
entries.20:7: A good person lives honestly, and his children after him are blessed. Your integrity is a gift that helps your family long after you.
entries.20:8: A king sitting in judgment sees through evil and drives it away. Those in charge should use their position to expose and stop wrongdoing.
entries.20:9: No one can honestly claim to have a completely clean heart and no sin at all. Everyone has done wrong, so be humble rather than pretending you are perfect.
entries.20:10: Cheating with dishonest weights and measures is hateful to the Lord. God cares about fairness in business, so don't cheat people to gain a little.
entries.20:11: You can tell what a child is really like by how he behaves, whether his actions are right and honest. Watch what children do, not just what they say.
entries.20:12: Both the ear that hears and the eye that sees are made by the Lord. Be thankful for your senses and use them to notice what is good.
entries.20:13: If you love sleep too much you will end up poor, but if you stay awake and work you will have enough to eat. Get up and do your part instead of being lazy.
entries.20:14: A buyer says the goods are worthless to get a lower price, then goes off boasting about the bargain. Don't be fooled by people who talk down a thing just to get their way.
entries.20:15: Gold and jewels are valuable, but words of knowledge are worth even more. Learning to speak wisely is a treasure greater than money.
entries.20:16: If someone guarantees a stranger's debt, take his coat as security and hold him to his promise. Be careful about promising to pay for someone you don't know.
entries.20:17: Food gained by cheating tastes sweet at first, but later it turns to grit in your mouth. Dishonest gain may feel good now, but it will leave you sorry.
entries.20:18: Good plans succeed when you get wise advice, and you should seek guidance before going to war. Don't make big decisions alone; ask people with wisdom.
entries.20:19: A person who gossips about others' business leaks secrets, so stay away from someone who talks too much. Don't trust a blabbermouth with anything private.
entries.20:20: Anyone who curses his father or mother will have his light put out in total darkness. Treating your parents with contempt brings serious trouble on yourself.
entries.20:21: Money or property gotten too quickly at first will not turn out to be a blessing in the end. Be patient about gaining wealth, because shortcuts often end badly.
entries.20:22: Don't say you will get even with someone for the wrong they did; wait for the Lord, and he will rescue you. Leave revenge to God and trust him to make things right.
entries.20:23: Dishonest weights are hateful to the Lord, and false scales are not good. God hates cheating in trade, so deal honestly with people.
entries.20:24: The Lord directs a person's steps, so how can anyone fully know his own way? Plan as you like, but trust God to guide where your life goes.
entries.20:25: It is dangerous to make a rash promise to give something to God and then later wonder whether you must keep it. Think before you promise, because you should keep your word.
entries.20:26: A wise king scatters evildoers and turns their own wickedness back on them. Good leadership deals firmly with wrongdoing instead of ignoring it.
entries.20:27: The Lord watches over the human spirit and searches out the deepest parts of a person. Nothing inside you is hidden from God, so live honestly before him.
entries.20:28: Kindness and faithfulness keep a king safe, and his rule is held up by doing what is right. Leaders stay strong through mercy and honesty, not through harshness.
entries.20:29: Young men are admired for their strength, and old men are honored for their gray hair. Each stage of life has its own value, so respect both the young and the old.
entries.20:30: Painful punishment can drive out evil and clean a person up deep inside. Sometimes hard consequences are what it takes to correct someone and make them change.
entries.21:1: A king may seem to do whatever he wants, but God quietly steers his decisions like a farmer directing a stream of water. So no human ruler is beyond God's control, and you can trust God to guide events.
entries.21:2: We usually think our own choices are obviously right, but we can't see our own hearts clearly. God can, so it's wise to ask him to show you where you're fooling yourself.
entries.21:3: God cares more about you treating people fairly and honestly than about any religious gift or ceremony you offer. Doing right in daily life pleases him more than impressive rituals.
entries.21:4: Arrogance, a proud look, and a haughty heart are sin, not just bad manners. God sees pride as wrongdoing, so watch for it in yourself.
entries.21:5: Hard work and careful planning tend to lead to plenty, while rushing and cutting corners tends to lead to lack. Patience and diligence pay off.
entries.21:6: Wealth gained by lying is empty and leads toward ruin. Dishonest gain is not worth having, because it costs you in the end.
entries.21:7: Violent people are eventually caught by their own violence, because they refuse to do what is right. Cruelty destroys the one who practices it.
entries.21:8: A guilty person's path is crooked, but a person with a clean heart does work that is straight and honest. Your inner character shows up in how you act.
entries.21:9: It's better to live alone in a cramped corner than in a big house with someone who constantly argues and criticizes. Peace at home matters more than comfort or space.
entries.21:10: A wicked person wants evil and has no kindness toward his neighbor. Watch out for desires that make you hard-hearted toward others.
entries.21:11: When a proud person is punished, a simple observer learns a lesson, and watching wise people adds knowledge. You can learn wisdom from other people's mistakes and examples.
entries.21:12: God, who is upright, watches over the wicked person's household and brings sinners down to ruin. God sees evil and does not let it stand forever.
entries.21:13: If you ignore the cries of the poor, your own cries for help will go unanswered. How you treat people in need affects how you'll be treated.
entries.21:14: A quiet gift can calm anger and a discreet present can cool hot tempers. A gentle, private gesture often defuses conflict better than a confrontation.
entries.21:15: Doing right brings joy to a good person, but it spells ruin for those who do evil. Right living is a delight to the honest and a threat to the wicked.
entries.21:16: Someone who wanders away from the path of knowledge will end up among the dead. Staying on the path of wisdom keeps you from ruin.
entries.21:17: Someone who chases pleasure, wine, and luxury will end up poor. Loving comfort and indulgence costs you in the long run.
entries.21:18: The wicked end up paying the price in place of the good, and the deceitful in place of the upright. In the end, evil catches up with those who practice it.
entries.21:19: It's better to live alone in a barren place than with a quarrelsome, angry person. Peace is worth more than company, even if it means being alone.
entries.21:20: A wise person's home holds valuable supplies, but a foolish person squanders them. Saving and managing what you have is wisdom; wasting it is folly.
entries.21:21: Whoever pursues right living and kindness will find life, goodness, and honor. Chase after what is right and merciful, and good things follow.
entries.21:22: A wise person can overcome a strong city and bring down the defenses people trust in. Wisdom is more powerful than sheer strength.
entries.21:23: If you guard what you say, you keep yourself out of trouble. Watching your words protects you from many problems.
entries.21:24: A proud, arrogant person is known as a mocker, and he acts with bold, reckless pride. Pride shows itself in how someone treats others.
entries.21:25: A lazy person's cravings destroy him because he refuses to work. Wanting things without doing the work only leads to ruin.
entries.21:26: A sinful person craves things all day long, but a righteous person gives generously and holds nothing back. Greed takes, while goodness gives.
entries.21:27: God finds the offerings of wicked people disgusting, especially when they bring them with bad motives. Religious gestures from an evil heart don't impress God.
entries.21:28: A lying witness will be cut off and come to nothing. Dishonesty in what you testify will eventually be exposed and punished.
entries.21:29: A wicked person puts on a bold, hard face, but an upright person thinks carefully about his path. Confidence without honesty is a mask; wisdom considers its steps.
entries.21:30: No wisdom, insight, or clever plan can succeed against the Lord. Human cleverness can't outsmart God, so it's foolish to fight against him.
entries.21:31: People prepare horses for battle, but victory comes from the Lord. Do your planning and preparation, but remember that the outcome is in God's hands.
entries.22:1: Being well thought of and trusted matters more than being rich. What people think of your character is worth more than money.
entries.22:2: Rich and poor people meet every day, and God made both of them. So treat everyone with respect, no matter their money.
entries.22:3: A wise person sees trouble coming and avoids it, while a careless person walks right into it. Pay attention to danger instead of ignoring it.
entries.22:4: Being humble and respecting God brings honor, a good life, and what you truly need. True reward comes from a humble heart, not from chasing things.
entries.22:5: People who do wrong run into traps and pain, but whoever guards their life stays away from them. Watch your path so you don't get caught in trouble.
entries.22:6: Start a child in the right direction early. What is planted young tends to stay planted.
entries.22:7: The rich often have power over the poor, and anyone who borrows becomes tied to the one who lent. Be careful about debt, because it can put you under someone else's control.
entries.22:8: Sowing evil brings a harvest of trouble, and the power to hurt others will not last. What you do comes back to you.
entries.22:9: A kind person who shares food with the poor will be blessed. Generosity toward those in need brings good to you as well.
entries.22:10: Remove a proud, mocking person and the arguing and fighting stop. Sometimes peace comes from not keeping troublemakers close.
entries.22:11: Someone with a pure heart and gracious words is loved by God and welcomed by leaders. Clean character and kind speech open doors.
entries.22:12: God watches over what is true and brings down the plans of liars. Honesty is protected, and deceit does not win in the end.
entries.22:13: A lazy person makes up excuses, saying there's a lion outside, to avoid doing anything. Excuses keep you from work and from what you should do.
entries.22:14: The seductive words of an immoral woman are like a trap, and those who turn from God fall into it. Be careful, because temptation can pull you down.
entries.22:15: Children naturally do foolish things, but loving discipline helps drive that foolishness out. Correcting a child is part of helping them grow right.
entries.22:16: Taking advantage of the poor to get rich, or flattering the wealthy, ends in loss. Unfair gain and wrong favors do not bring lasting good.
entries.22:17: Listen closely and think carefully about wise words. Paying attention to wisdom is worth your effort.
entries.22:18: It's a joy to keep wise words in your heart and ready on your tongue. Let good teaching stay with you so you can use it.
entries.22:19: These teachings are given so your trust can rest in the Lord. Wisdom is meant to lead you to trust God, not just to know facts.
entries.22:20: These are written-down wise sayings meant to give you knowledge. Take time to learn from collected wisdom.
entries.22:21: These true words help you give honest, reliable answers to people who ask you. Knowing what is true helps you speak truthfully.
entries.22:22: Don't rob a poor person just because they are weak, or crush someone in court. Protect the vulnerable instead of taking advantage of them.
entries.22:23: God will defend the cause of the poor and punish those who take from them. God sees injustice and stands with those who are mistreated.
entries.22:24: Don't become close friends with someone who is quick to anger. Angry companions can pull you into their ways.
entries.22:25: You might learn their angry habits and get trapped by them yourself. Bad company can shape you in ways that hurt you.
entries.22:26: Don't be quick to shake hands on deals or promise to pay someone else's debt. Be careful about taking on obligations that could ruin you.
entries.22:27: If you can't pay, the lender may take even your bed from under you. Don't promise what you can't afford to lose.
entries.22:28: Don't move property markers that your ancestors set. Respect what was established before you and don't take what isn't yours.
entries.22:29: Someone skilled at their work will serve before kings, not stay among ordinary people. Doing your work well brings honor and opens doors.
entries.23:1: Be careful and pay attention when you eat with an important person. Watch how you act and what you take, because the situation matters.
entries.23:2: If you are greedy for food, control yourself sharply, even as if your life depended on it. Your appetite can get you into trouble, so master it.
entries.23:3: Don't crave the fancy food such a person offers, because it may come with hidden motives. What looks generous can be a trap.
entries.23:4: Don't wear yourself out chasing wealth. Stop making money the thing you long for.
entries.23:5: The moment you look at wealth, it can vanish like an eagle flying away. Money is unreliable, so don't set your heart on it.
entries.23:6: Don't accept food from a stingy, grudging person, and don't crave his fancy dishes. His generosity isn't real.
entries.23:7: A person is really like his inner thoughts, so when he says eat and drink but doesn't mean it, you can't trust him. Judge people by what's in their heart, not their words.
entries.23:8: You'll regret the meal and feel sick over it, and your kind words to him will be wasted. Don't invest in a relationship with someone who is fake.
entries.23:9: Don't bother giving advice to a fool, because he'll dismiss your wise words. Save your wisdom for those willing to hear it.
entries.23:10: Don't move a widow's boundary marker or take over land that belongs to orphans. Respect the property and rights of the vulnerable.
entries.23:11: Their defender is strong and will plead their case against you. God himself stands up for those who can't protect themselves.
entries.23:12: Commit yourself to learning and listen carefully to words that give knowledge. Growth comes from a willing heart and open ears.
entries.23:13: Don't hold back discipline from a child; correction won't kill him. Loving discipline is part of raising a child well.
entries.23:14: Discipline your child, and you rescue him from a destructive path. Correction can save a life.
entries.23:15: If your heart grows wise, I will be deeply glad. Your wisdom brings real joy to those who care about you.
entries.23:16: I will rejoice when you speak what is right. Honest, upright words from you are a delight to hear.
entries.23:17: Don't envy those who do wrong, but keep honoring the Lord all day long. Reverence for God is better than longing for what sinners have.
entries.23:18: There is surely a future ahead, and your hope will not be crushed. Living rightly is worth it because hope lies ahead.
entries.23:19: Listen, and be wise, and steer your heart in the right direction. Wisdom starts with paying attention and choosing your path carefully.
entries.23:20: Don't join those who drink too much wine or stuff themselves with meat. Avoid the company of people given to excess.
entries.23:21: Drunkards and gluttons end up poor, and too much sleep leaves you in rags. Self-indulgence costs you in the end.
entries.23:22: Listen to your father, who raised you, and don't dishonor your mother when she is old. Honor your parents for life.
entries.23:23: Buy the truth and never sell it; get wisdom, instruction, and understanding. Truth and wisdom are worth more than money.
entries.23:24: A father of a righteous person is glad, and a wise child brings joy. Your good character makes your parents happy.
entries.23:25: Bring gladness to your father and mother, and joy to the one who gave you birth. Let your life be a gift to your parents.
entries.23:26: Give me your whole heart, and let your eyes take pleasure in my ways. Real teaching asks for your heart, not just your attention.
entries.23:27: A promiscuous woman is like a deep pit or a narrow well—easy to fall into and hard to escape. Such a path traps a person.
entries.23:28: She waits in ambush like a predator and multiplies unfaithfulness among people. This kind of temptation quietly ruins many.
entries.23:29: Who has sorrow, grief, fights, and unexplained wounds, and bloodshot eyes? These are the marks of a life gone wrong.
entries.23:30: It's those who linger long over wine and keep seeking mixed drinks. Too much drinking leaves its visible damage.
entries.23:31: Don't stare at wine when it's red and sparkling and goes down smoothly. What looks appealing can be dangerous.
entries.23:32: In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper. The pleasure of drink hides a painful poison.
entries.23:33: Your eyes will see strange things and your mouth will say twisted things. Drink distorts how you see and speak.
entries.23:34: You'll feel like someone lying down in the middle of the sea or on top of a mast. You become dizzy and helpless, in real danger.
entries.23:35: You'll say they hit you but you felt nothing, and you'll wonder when you'll wake up so you can go after more. Addiction keeps pulling a person back even after it hurts them.
entries.24:1: Don't wish you had what evil people have, and don't want to spend time with them. Wanting their life pulls you toward their ways.
entries.24:2: Their minds are set on tearing things down, and their talk stirs up trouble. Being close to them means hearing and absorbing that.
entries.24:3: A home is built well through wisdom, and it stands firm through good sense. Lasting homes come from thoughtful choices, not luck.
entries.24:4: Knowledge fills a house with good and pleasant things. Learning and understanding bring real value to everyday life.
entries.24:5: A wise person has real strength, and knowledge adds to it. Wisdom makes you more capable, not less.
entries.24:6: Good advice wins battles, and having many wise counselors brings safety. Don't try to figure everything out alone.
entries.24:7: Wisdom is out of reach for a fool, so he stays quiet when leaders meet. Sometimes not speaking is the only safe option for someone who hasn't learned.
entries.24:8: Someone who plans evil will get a reputation as a schemer. What you plot privately becomes how people see you.
entries.24:9: Foolish planning leads to sin, and a person who resents correction is disliked. Attitude and actions go together.
entries.24:10: If you collapse when trouble comes, your strength was never much. Hard days show what you're really made of.
entries.24:11: Rescue people who are being led to death, and don't hold back help from those about to be destroyed. When you can save someone, you should.
entries.24:12: Don't claim you didn't know; God sees hearts and knows what you really knew, and he will repay each person fairly. You can't hide behind excuses with him.
entries.24:13: Honey is good and sweet to eat. This is a simple picture of something pleasant and worth having.
entries.24:14: In the same way, make wisdom your goal; if you have it, you'll have a future and your hope won't be cut off. Wisdom pays off in the long run.
entries.24:15: Don't lurk and plot against a good person's home or land. Attacking the upright is wrong, even in secret.
entries.24:16: A good person may fall seven times and still get back up, but trouble brings the wicked down for good. Falling isn't the end for the upright; getting up is what matters.
entries.24:17: Don't celebrate when someone who hates you falls. Enjoying another's downfall is not the way of wisdom.
entries.24:18: God may see your gloating and dislike it, and turn his anger away from that person. Your attitude can change how things go.
entries.24:19: Don't get upset over evildoers or wish you were like sinners. Their apparent success shouldn't disturb your peace.
entries.24:20: Evil people have no future, and their light will go out. Whatever they seem to have now won't last.
entries.24:21: Honor the Lord and the king, and don't join up with people who stir up rebellion. Respect for proper authority keeps you out of danger.
entries.24:22: Disaster can hit such people suddenly, and no one knows what ruin may come. Rebels can fall fast and hard.
entries.24:23: These are more wise sayings: it's wrong to favor someone in court just because of who they are. Fair judgment means not playing favorites.
entries.24:24: Anyone who tells a guilty person they're innocent will be cursed and hated by whole peoples. Calling wrong right brings public shame.
entries.24:25: Those who confront the guilty will be glad, and good blessings will come on them. Speaking the truth, even when hard, brings reward.
entries.24:26: A right answer is like a friendly kiss. Honest, fitting words build closeness and trust.
entries.24:27: Get your outdoor work and field ready first, then build your house. Do things in the right order and secure your income before bigger projects.
entries.24:28: Don't testify violently or falsely against your neighbor. Don't use your words to harm someone nearby.
entries.24:29: Don't say you'll pay someone back for what they did to you. Revenge belongs to God, not to you.
entries.24:30: I walked past the field of a lazy man and the vineyard of a foolish person. Watching careless people teaches you something.
entries.24:31: It was full of thorns and weeds, and its stone wall had fallen down. Neglect shows up visibly over time.
entries.24:32: I looked, thought about it, and learned a lesson from what I saw. Other people's mistakes can be your teachers.
entries.24:33: A little sleep, a little rest, a little folding of your hands. Small laziness adds up.
entries.24:34: Then poverty comes on you like a robber, and need like an armed man. Neglect invites sudden loss you can't stop.
entries.25:1: This verse notes that these proverbs were collected and copied by King Hezekiah's officials. It reminds the reader that wisdom is worth preserving and passing on carefully.
entries.25:2: God is honored by what He keeps hidden, while kings are honored by searching out the truth. It means leaders should work hard to uncover facts rather than guess.
entries.25:3: Just as no one can measure the height of the sky or the depth of the earth, no one can fully read a king's mind. It reminds us that people in power are not always easy to understand.
entries.25:4: Removing impurities from silver lets the craftsman make something useful. In the same way, removing what is wrong makes room for something good to be made.
entries.25:5: When a king removes wicked people from his court, his rule becomes strong and fair. It means good leadership requires getting rid of corruption.
entries.25:6: Don't push yourself forward in front of important people or act as if you belong among the great. It's a warning against self-promotion.
entries.25:7: It is better to be invited up to a higher place than to be told to move down in front of a ruler. It teaches humility, letting others honor you rather than claiming honor yourself.
entries.25:8: Don't rush to court over something you have seen, because you may end up embarrassed if your neighbor proves you wrong. It advises thinking carefully before starting a public dispute.
entries.25:9: Talk directly with your neighbor about your disagreement, but don't reveal someone else's secret. It means handle conflict honestly and privately without betraying trust.
entries.25:10: If you betray a secret, the person who hears it may speak badly of you, and your reputation will be damaged. It warns that loose talk has lasting consequences.
entries.25:11: A well-chosen word at the right moment is beautiful and valuable, like gold decorations set in silver. It encourages us to speak carefully and at the right time.
entries.25:12: A wise person who corrects someone willing to listen is as valuable as fine gold jewelry. It means good advice is a treasure when we are humble enough to receive it.
entries.25:13: A reliable messenger refreshes the one who sent him, like cool snow on a hot harvest day. It means being dependable brings real relief and joy to those who trust you.
entries.25:14: Someone who promises a gift but never gives it is like clouds and wind that bring no rain. It means empty promises disappoint people and are worthless.
entries.25:15: Patience and gentle words can persuade even a stubborn judge. It means staying calm and speaking softly is more powerful than pushing hard.
entries.25:16: Eat only as much honey as you need, or you will get sick of it. It teaches moderation, even with good things.
entries.25:17: Don't visit your neighbor's house too often, or he may grow tired of you and start to dislike you. It means respect people's space and don't wear out your welcome.
entries.25:18: A person who lies about his neighbor in court hurts him like a hammer, a sword, or a sharp arrow. It shows how damaging false accusations really are.
entries.25:19: Trusting an unreliable person when trouble comes is like biting on a broken tooth or standing on a shaky foot. It means depending on the wrong person only adds pain.
entries.25:20: Singing cheerful songs to someone with a heavy heart is as hurtful as taking off their coat in the cold or pouring acid on a wound. It means be sensitive to people who are grieving.
entries.25:21: If someone who hates you is hungry or thirsty, give them food and water. It means respond to hostility with kindness instead of revenge.
entries.25:22: Being kind to an enemy is like piling hot coals on his head, and God will reward you. It means kindness can soften a hard heart, and God sees and honors it.
entries.25:23: A north wind brings rain, and secret gossip stirs up angry looks. It means talking behind someone's back causes real trouble and hurt feelings.
entries.25:24: It is better to live alone in a tiny corner of the roof than in a big house with a wife who constantly argues. It means peace matters more than comfort or space.
entries.25:25: Good news from a distant place refreshes a weary person like cold water on a hot day. It means hopeful news can deeply restore someone who is worn out.
entries.25:26: When a good person gives in to wicked people, it is like a spring that has been muddied or polluted. It means compromise by good people damages the good they could do for others.
entries.25:27: Eating too much honey isn't good for you, and neither is chasing honor for yourself. It means seeking praise too hard is unhealthy, while humility is better.
entries.25:28: A person who can't control his temper is like a city with broken-down walls, open to attack. It means self-control protects you, and losing it leaves you vulnerable.
entries.26:1: Snow in summer and rain at harvest are out of place and harmful, and so is honour given to a fool. It reminds the reader that praise and respect should go to those who deserve them, not to people who will only misuse them.
entries.26:2: A bird flying around does not land just anywhere, and in the same way a curse spoken without a real reason does not settle on anyone. The reader can take comfort that words spoken against them unfairly have no real power.
entries.26:3: A horse needs a whip and a donkey needs a bit, and a stubborn fool only learns through firm correction. It means some people will not respond to reason and need tougher handling.
entries.26:4: If you answer a fool in the same foolish way he talks, you sink to his level. The reader should not let a foolish person pull them into a silly argument.
entries.26:5: Sometimes you do need to answer a fool in a way that exposes his foolishness, or he will walk away thinking he was right. The point is to correct him so he does not become proud of his nonsense.
entries.26:6: Trusting a fool to deliver a message is like hurting yourself and asking for trouble. The reader should not hand important tasks to someone who will botch them.
entries.26:7: A wise saying means nothing in a fool's mouth, just as legs that cannot walk are useless. Good words only help when the person speaking them actually lives by them.
entries.26:8: Honouring a fool is as pointless as tying a stone into a sling, where it will not stay. Respect given to the wrong person is wasted and does no good.
entries.26:9: A wise saying in a fool's mouth is like a thorn in a drunk man's hand, painful and misused. The reader should be careful that good words are not twisted by people who do not understand them.
entries.26:10: A drunk man with a bow hurts everyone around him, and so does a fool who lashes out. It warns the reader to stay clear of people whose foolishness causes random harm.
entries.26:11: A dog returns to its vomit, and a fool keeps repeating the same stupid mistakes. The reader is urged to learn from their errors instead of going back to them.
entries.26:12: Someone who thinks he is already wise is harder to help than a plain fool. The reader should stay humble and open to learning, because thinking you know it all is the worst trap.
entries.26:13: The lazy person makes excuses, claiming there is a lion outside so he cannot go out. It shows how people invent reasons to avoid work and responsibility.
entries.26:14: A door swings on its hinge without going anywhere, and a lazy person turns over in bed the same way. The reader is warned against endless rest that never leads to action.
entries.26:15: The lazy person puts his hand in the dish but finds it too much effort to lift food to his mouth. It pictures how laziness makes even simple, necessary things seem too hard.
entries.26:16: The lazy person thinks he is wiser than seven sensible people put together. It warns the reader that laziness often comes with a false confidence that keeps a person stuck.
entries.26:17: Grabbing a passing dog by the ears gets you bitten, and butting into a quarrel that is not yours does the same. The reader should stay out of other people's fights.
entries.26:18: A madman who throws fire and deadly arrows around hurts people without thinking. It describes someone who causes damage and then acts as if it were nothing.
entries.26:19: Someone who tricks his neighbour and then says it was only a joke is like that madman. The reader should not excuse real harm by calling it fun.
entries.26:20: Fire goes out when there is no wood, and arguments stop when people stop gossiping. The reader can end a quarrel by refusing to pass on secret talk.
entries.26:21: Just as air feeds coals and wood feeds a fire, a quarrelsome person keeps a fight going. The reader is warned not to be the one who stirs up trouble.
entries.26:22: Gossip about others tastes sweet and goes deep inside a person. It warns the reader that secret slander is tempting to hear but does real damage.
entries.26:23: Kind words covering a hateful heart are like a cheap clay pot painted to look like silver. The reader should look past smooth talk and judge people by what is really inside.
entries.26:24: A person who hates you may talk nicely while hiding deceit inside. The reader should not be fooled by pleasant words when someone's actions show otherwise.
entries.26:25: When such a person speaks kindly, do not believe him, because his heart is full of evil plans. The reader is warned to be careful with charming talk that hides bad intentions.
entries.26:26: Even if hatred is hidden for a while, the wrong will eventually become clear to everyone. The reader can trust that hidden evil does not stay hidden forever.
entries.26:27: Whoever digs a pit for someone else falls into it, and the stone you roll at others comes back on you. It means the harm you plan for others tends to land on yourself.
entries.26:28: A lying tongue hurts people with honest hearts, and smooth flattery leads to ruin. The reader should value truth and beware of words that are too smooth to be trusted.
entries.27:1: Don't brag about what you'll do tomorrow, because you don't know what will happen. Plan ahead, but hold your plans loosely and stay humble about the future.
entries.27:2: Let other people praise you instead of praising yourself. When you boast about your own good qualities, it sounds better coming from someone else.
entries.27:3: A heavy stone and a load of sand are hard to carry, but a fool's anger is even harder to bear. Be careful not to be the person whose temper weighs everyone down.
entries.27:4: Anger is cruel and can flood over people like a river, but envy is even worse and harder to stand against. Watch your envy, because it can do more damage than plain anger.
entries.27:5: It's better to tell someone honestly when something is wrong than to keep quiet and call it love. Real love is willing to speak up instead of hiding problems.
entries.27:6: A friend who hurts you is still being honest and trustworthy, but an enemy's kind words are fake. Accept honest correction from friends and don't be fooled by flattery.
entries.27:7: When you're full, even honey looks unappealing, but when you're starving, even bitter food tastes good. Our circumstances change how we see things, so be mindful of people who are in need.
entries.27:8: A bird that wanders far from its nest is like a person who leaves the place where they belong. Stay grounded where you have responsibilities and community.
entries.27:9: Oil and perfume cheer people up, and so does good advice from a friend. Good friends who give wise counsel are a real comfort to the soul.
entries.27:10: Don't abandon your own friend or your family's old friends, and don't count on a distant relative in a crisis. A nearby neighbor you can rely on is better than family far away.
entries.27:11: Be wise, and it will make your parents glad and give them an answer to those who criticize them. Your good choices reflect well on the people who raised you.
entries.27:12: A wise person sees danger coming and takes cover, but a naive person walks right into trouble. Pay attention to warning signs and act before problems hit.
entries.27:13: If someone promises to pay a stranger's debt, take their coat as security until they pay. Be cautious about guaranteeing loans for people you don't know.
entries.27:14: If you loudly bless your friend early in the morning, it may be taken as a curse rather than a blessing. Timing matters, so don't be loud and intrusive even when you mean well.
entries.27:15: A woman with a bitter tongue is like constant dripping on a rainy day. A nagging, harsh way of speaking wears people down and makes home miserable.
entries.27:16: Whoever keeps a friend's secret earns a reputation for being trustworthy. Being reliable with confidences is how you build a good name.
entries.27:17: Iron sharpens iron, and in the same way one person sharpens another. Good friends challenge and improve each other.
entries.27:18: Whoever tends a fig tree gets to eat its fruit, and a servant who looks after his master will be honored. Faithful work and care for what's entrusted to you will be rewarded.
entries.27:19: Just as water reflects a face back to you, so people's hearts reflect one another. We can learn about ourselves by paying attention to others.
entries.27:20: The grave and destruction are never satisfied, and human eyes are never satisfied either. Greed and endless wanting will never be filled, so guard your heart against it.
entries.27:21: A furnace tests silver and gold, and a person is tested by the praise they receive. How you handle compliments shows what kind of person you really are.
entries.27:22: Even if you grind a fool up like grain with a hammer, his foolishness won't leave him. Some people won't change no matter how hard you try, so don't be surprised when they don't.
entries.27:23: Be diligent to know how your flocks are doing and take good care of your herds. Pay attention to the things you're responsible for, because good management matters.
entries.27:24: Riches don't last forever, and money doesn't continue through every generation. Don't put your whole trust in wealth, because it can disappear.
entries.27:25: The grass grows, new plants appear, and the mountain herbs are gathered in. There's a natural rhythm to work and provision, so do your part in season.
entries.27:26: The lambs provide you with clothing, and the goats can be sold to buy a field. Your work and resources can meet your needs and build for the future.
entries.27:27: There will be enough goat's milk for your food and for the young women who work for you. Take care of your household and workers, and God provides through honest labor.
entries.28:1: A guilty person runs away even when nobody is chasing him, while an honest person can be brave like a lion. If you live honestly, you don't have to live in fear.
entries.28:2: A land falls into chaos because of its sin, but wise and understanding leaders can calm it down. Good leadership and wisdom can bring order to a troubled situation.
entries.28:3: A rich person who crushes the poor is like a downpour that washes away the crops people need. Using your power to hurt those who depend on you destroys what should feed them.
entries.28:4: People who ignore the law cheer on wrongdoers, but those who obey the law stand against them. Your attitude toward God's rules shows whose side you are really on.
entries.28:5: Wicked people don't understand what is right, but those who seek the Lord understand everything they need to. Following God gives you real insight into right and wrong.
entries.28:6: A poor person who lives honestly is better off than a rich person who cheats. Character matters more than money.
entries.28:7: A son who follows the law makes his father proud, but one who hangs around with wild partiers brings him shame. The friends you choose affect how you honor your family.
entries.28:8: Someone who gets rich by charging unfair interest is really just piling up money for someone who will be generous to the poor. Dishonest gain doesn't stay with you.
entries.28:9: If someone refuses to listen to God's law, even his prayers are offensive to God. You can't ignore what God says and expect him to hear you.
entries.28:10: Anyone who leads good people into evil will fall into his own trap, but honest people will receive good things. Leading others astray backfires on the one who does it.
entries.28:11: A rich man thinks he is wise, but a poor person with understanding sees right through him. Wealth doesn't make you smart, and humble insight can see what money can't.
entries.28:12: When good people succeed, everyone celebrates, but when the wicked rise to power, people hide. The kind of leaders in charge affects how safe everyone feels.
entries.28:13: Hiding your sins doesn't work out, but admitting them and turning away from them brings mercy. Being honest about your wrongs is the path to forgiveness.
entries.28:14: A person who always respects the Lord is happy, but one who hardens his heart gets into trouble. Keeping a tender, reverent heart keeps you out of trouble.
entries.28:15: A wicked ruler over poor people is like a roaring lion or a charging bear. Bad leaders are dangerous to those who are weakest.
entries.28:16: A ruler without understanding is cruel, but one who hates dishonest gain will live long. Greedy, foolish leaders hurt people, while honest ones last.
entries.28:17: Someone guilty of murder runs toward the grave, and no one should help him escape. A person who has taken a life carries a burden that shouldn't be lightened.
entries.28:18: Whoever walks honestly will be kept safe, but the crooked will suddenly fall. Integrity protects you, while dishonesty brings a sudden downfall.
entries.28:19: Working your land brings plenty of food, but chasing worthless pursuits leaves you poor. Hard work pays off, while chasing fantasies doesn't.
entries.28:20: A faithful person is greatly blessed, but someone trying to get rich fast won't escape punishment. Slow, honest effort is blessed, while get-rich-quick schemes bring trouble.
entries.28:21: It's wrong to show favoritism, because people will do wrong even for a small bribe. Playing favorites and taking bribes corrupts justice.
entries.28:22: A person greedy for wealth chases money and doesn't realize poverty is coming for him. Greed blinds you to the loss it is bringing.
entries.28:23: Someone who honestly corrects a person will be appreciated more in the end than one who just flatters. Honest correction is better than smooth talk, even if it stings at first.
entries.28:24: A person who robs his father or mother and says it's no big deal is as bad as a murderer. Cheating your own parents and excusing it is serious evil.
entries.28:25: A greedy person stirs up conflict, but whoever trusts the Lord will be satisfied. Greed causes fights, while trust in God brings contentment.
entries.28:26: Trusting only in yourself is foolish, but whoever walks wisely will be kept safe. Don't rely on your own judgment alone; live wisely and you'll be protected.
entries.28:27: Whoever gives to the poor will never lack, but whoever ignores them will be cursed. Generosity to the needy is repaid, while neglect brings trouble.
entries.28:28: When the wicked rise to power, people hide, but when they fall, good people come out and grow. Good people flourish when evil leaders are gone.
entries.29:1: Someone who refuses correction and hardens himself against it will one day be ruined with no chance to recover. It warns the reader to stay teachable rather than stubborn.
entries.29:2: People are happy when good leaders are in charge, but they suffer when a wicked person rules. It reminds the reader that leadership affects everyone's daily life.
entries.29:3: A son who loves wisdom brings his father joy, while one who chases after loose women wastes money. It shows the reader that wise choices bless family and foolish choices drain resources.
entries.29:4: A king who rules justly brings stability to the land, but one driven by greed ruins it. It tells the reader that fair leadership builds safety while selfish leadership destroys.
entries.29:5: Flattering a neighbor with smooth talk is really setting a trap for him. It warns the reader that false praise can harm the person who receives it.
entries.29:6: An evil person gets caught in his own trap, but a good person escapes quickly and rejoices. It encourages the reader that integrity leads to freedom and joy.
entries.29:7: A good person cares about justice for the poor, while a wicked person doesn't even think about it. It challenges the reader to notice and care for those in need.
entries.29:8: Arrogant people stir up violence in a city, but wise people calm anger down. It tells the reader that humility and wisdom can prevent conflict.
entries.29:9: When a wise man argues with a fool, whether the fool rages or laughs, there is no peace. It warns the reader that some arguments are pointless and exhausting.
entries.29:10: Violent people hate those who do good and seek to destroy them. It reminds the reader that doing right may bring opposition from those who love wrong.
entries.29:11: A fool blurts out all his anger, but a wise person holds it back quietly. It encourages the reader to control their temper instead of venting everything.
entries.29:12: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials become wicked. It warns the reader that leaders who tolerate deceit corrupt everyone under them.
entries.29:13: The poor and the rich both owe their life and sight to the Lord, who treats them equally. It reminds the reader that God values every person the same, regardless of wealth.
entries.29:14: A king who judges the poor fairly will have a secure throne forever. It tells the reader that justice for the vulnerable is the foundation of lasting leadership.
entries.29:15: Discipline and correction give wisdom, but a child left undisciplined brings shame to his mother. It encourages the reader to accept that loving correction is necessary for growth.
entries.29:16: When wicked people gain power, wrongdoing increases, but good people will eventually see them fall and be glad. It gives the reader hope that evil will not win forever.
entries.29:17: Discipline your son and he will give you peace and delight. It encourages the reader that patient training of children pays off in rest and joy.
entries.29:18: Without guidance from God, people run wild, but whoever follows God's law is happy. It tells the reader that God's instruction brings order and blessing.
entries.29:19: A servant won't be corrected by words alone; even if he understands, he won't pay attention. It warns the reader that some people need more than talk to change.
entries.29:20: Someone who speaks too quickly has less hope than a fool. It cautions the reader to think before speaking rather than rush to talk.
entries.29:21: A servant pampered from youth will end up causing grief. It warns the reader that overindulgence without boundaries can spoil a person.
entries.29:22: An angry person starts fights, and a hot-tempered person does much wrong. It encourages the reader to deal with anger before it causes damage.
entries.29:23: Pride brings a person down, but a humble spirit receives honor. It tells the reader that humility lifts people up while arrogance leads to a fall.
entries.29:24: Partnering with a thief harms yourself; when questioned under oath, you stay silent and share the guilt. It warns the reader not to cover for wrongdoing.
entries.29:25: Fearing what people think is a trap, but trusting the Lord keeps you safe. It encourages the reader to put confidence in God rather than in others' approval.
entries.29:26: Many want a ruler's favor, but true justice comes from the Lord. It reminds the reader to look to God for what is right, not just to powerful people.
entries.29:27: Good people find evil people disgusting, and evil people find good people disgusting. It tells the reader that living rightly will naturally create tension with those who don't.
entries.30:1: Agur is worn out and admits he has reached his limit. It's okay to be honest with God when you feel exhausted and empty.
entries.30:2: He feels stupid and less than human in his understanding. We can admit our ignorance to God without pretending to be wise.
entries.30:3: He never learned wisdom or came to know God through his own study. Knowing God is a gift, not something we achieve by being smart.
entries.30:4: He asks who could possibly control the sky, wind, and sea or know God's name and his son's. These questions show that God is far beyond our grasp and we depend on him to reveal himself.
entries.30:5: God's words can be trusted because they have been tested, and he protects those who rely on him. You can count on what God says and feel safe trusting him.
entries.30:6: Don't add your own ideas to what God has said, or you will be exposed as wrong. Take God's words as they are rather than reshaping them to suit yourself.
entries.30:7: He asks God for two things before he dies. It's fine to bring God specific, honest requests about your life.
entries.30:8: He asks to be kept from lies and from both riches and poverty, wanting just enough food. Ask God for enough rather than chasing extremes.
entries.30:9: Too much could make him deny God, and too little could make him steal and dishonor God's name. Having just enough helps you stay faithful to God.
entries.30:10: Don't badmouth a servant to his master, or you may be cursed and get yourself in trouble. Be careful about stirring up trouble between people.
entries.30:11: Some people curse their father and refuse to bless their mother. Treating your parents with contempt is a serious wrong.
entries.30:12: Some people think they are pure but are still dirty inside. It's possible to fool yourself about your own sin.
entries.30:13: Some people are extremely proud, looking down on everyone. Pride shows in how you look at others.
entries.30:14: Some people use their words like knives to destroy the poor and needy. Cruel speech that crushes the vulnerable is evil.
entries.30:15: The leech has two daughters crying 'Give, give,' and four things are never satisfied. Greed is a hunger that never says 'enough.'
entries.30:16: The grave, a childless woman, dry ground, and fire are never satisfied. Some longings and forces in life simply cannot be filled or stopped.
entries.30:17: A child who mocks his father and despises his old mother will come to a bad end. Treating your parents with scorn brings serious consequences.
entries.30:18: He is amazed by three things, even four, that he cannot understand. It's fine to wonder at things beyond your understanding.
entries.30:19: An eagle in the sky, a snake on a rock, a ship at sea, and a man with a young woman leave no trace. Some things are mysterious and leave no obvious mark.
entries.30:20: A cheating wife eats, wipes her mouth, and claims she did nothing wrong. Some people do wrong and then act as if they are innocent.
entries.30:21: The earth cannot tolerate three things, even four. Some situations are deeply unsettling and out of place.
entries.30:22: A servant who becomes king and a fool who gets rich are hard to bear. Sudden power or wealth in the wrong hands causes trouble.
entries.30:23: An unloved woman who marries and a servant girl who replaces her mistress are hard to bear. Being raised suddenly to a place you were not expected to hold can cause upheaval.
entries.30:24: Four small creatures are very wise. Small and humble things can teach us real wisdom.
entries.30:25: Ants are weak but store food in summer. Planning ahead, even when you are small, is wise.
entries.30:26: Rock badgers are weak but make their homes in rocks. Finding a safe place to shelter is wisdom.
entries.30:27: Locusts have no king yet move together in ranks. Working together without a leader can be powerful.
entries.30:28: A lizard can be caught by hand yet lives in kings' palaces. Even the small and lowly can reach places of honor.
entries.30:29: Three things walk well, even four. Some things are simply impressive to watch.
entries.30:30: The lion is the strongest beast and does not back down from anything. Strength that does not retreat is impressive.
entries.30:31: A strutting rooster, a goat, and a king with his army are impressive in their stride. Confidence and order are good to see.
entries.30:32: If you have been foolish and proud or planned evil, cover your mouth and stop. When you catch yourself being arrogant or scheming, quiet down and stop.
entries.30:33: Churning milk makes butter and twisting a nose makes blood, and stirring up anger causes fights. If you keep pushing people's anger, conflict will come.
entries.31:1: This verse introduces wise advice that King Lemuel learned from his mother. It reminds readers that wisdom often comes from family, especially from a mother's teaching.
entries.31:2: His mother speaks tenderly to her son, calling him her own child and the answer to her prayers. It shows a mother's deep love and concern as she gives him guidance.
entries.31:3: She warns him not to waste his strength on women or on habits that ruin kings. Readers are reminded that careless desires can destroy even powerful people.
entries.31:4: She tells him that kings should not drink wine or crave strong drink. People with responsibility should stay clear-headed so they can lead well.
entries.31:5: Drinking can make a ruler forget the law and give unfair rulings against people in trouble. It warns that alcohol can cloud judgment and harm the vulnerable.
entries.31:6: Strong drink is meant for those who are dying or deeply bitter in spirit. It shows compassion for people in extreme pain.
entries.31:7: Such a person drinks to forget their misery and trouble for a while. It acknowledges that some people need relief from overwhelming sorrow.
entries.31:8: She urges him to speak up for people who have no voice and for those facing death. Readers are called to defend those who cannot defend themselves.
entries.31:9: He should speak up, judge fairly, and stand up for the poor and needy. It means using your position to help those who are overlooked.
entries.31:10: This begins a poem about a woman of strong character, asking who can find one. It says such a woman is worth more than jewels.
entries.31:11: Her husband trusts her completely, and because of her he lacks nothing. It shows how trust and reliability build a strong home.
entries.31:12: She brings her husband good, never harm, for as long as she lives. It describes steady faithfulness in a marriage.
entries.31:13: She gathers wool and flax and works with her hands willingly. It shows her as industrious and skilled in making what her family needs.
entries.31:14: She is compared to merchant ships that bring food from far away. It means she is resourceful in providing for her household.
entries.31:15: She rises before dawn to feed her family and her servants. It shows her dedication and care for everyone in her home.
entries.31:16: She carefully examines a field and buys it, then plants a vineyard with her earnings. It shows her good judgment and hard work paying off.
entries.31:17: She prepares herself for hard work and makes her arms strong. It pictures her as energetic and ready for labor.
entries.31:18: She sees that her business is profitable, and her lamp burns late into the night. It shows her commitment and diligence.
entries.31:19: She works with her hands at spinning cloth. It highlights her practical skill and steady labor.
entries.31:20: She reaches out to the poor and opens her hands to the needy. It shows her generosity and compassion toward those in need.
entries.31:21: She does not worry about snow for her household because everyone is warmly clothed. It shows her careful preparation for her family's needs.
entries.31:22: She makes fine coverings for herself and wears linen and purple. It shows dignity and quality in her work and appearance.
entries.31:23: Her husband is respected among the leaders at the city gate. It shows how her character adds to her family's honor.
entries.31:24: She makes linen garments and sells them, and supplies merchants with belts. It shows her as a capable businesswoman.
entries.31:25: She is clothed with strength and dignity and laughs at the days to come. It means she faces the future with confidence and joy.
entries.31:26: She speaks with wisdom, and kindness is on her tongue. It shows her words are thoughtful and gracious.
entries.31:27: She watches over her household and does not sit idle. It shows her as attentive and hardworking in caring for her home.
entries.31:28: Her children and husband rise up to honor and praise her. It shows the respect and gratitude her family gives her.
entries.31:29: Her husband tells her that many women have done well, but she surpasses them all. It is high praise for her outstanding character.
entries.31:30: Charm and beauty fade, but a woman who honors the Lord deserves praise. It teaches that character matters more than appearance.
entries.31:31: She should receive credit for her work, and her deeds should be praised publicly. It means good work deserves recognition and honor.
